28: # A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".

31: _OPEN = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
32: _CLOSE = {v: k for k, v in _OPEN.items()}

35: def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
36:     """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.
37: 
38:     Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
39:     unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
40:     with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
41:     said OK.
42:     """
43:     stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
44:     i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
45:     while i < n:
46:         c = text[i]
47:         if depth:                                  # inside a comment
48:             if text.startswith("(*", i):
49:                 depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
50:             elif text.startswith("*)", i):
51:                 depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
52:             else:
53:                 i += 1
54:             continue
55:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
56:             depth, i = 1, i + 2
57:             continue
58:         if c == '"':                               # string literal
59:             i += 1
60:             while i < n and text[i] != '"':
61:                 i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
62:             if i >= n:
63:                 return "unterminated string literal"
64:             i += 1
65:             continue
66:         if c in _OPEN:
67:             stack.append((c, i))
68:         elif c in _CLOSE:
69:             if not stack or stack[-1][0] != _CLOSE[c]:
70:                 ctx = text[max(0, i - 30):i + 1]
71:                 return f"unexpected '{c}' at character {i} (...{ctx})"
72:             stack.pop()
73:         i += 1
74:     if depth:
75:         return "unterminated comment"
76:     if stack:
77:         c, j = stack[-1]
78:         ctx = text[j:j + 30]
79:         return f"'{c}' at character {j} is never closed ({ctx}...)"
80:     return None

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )

190: \begin{abstract}
191: Leptoquarks (LQs) have attracted increasing attention within recent years, mainly since they can explain the flavor anomalies found in $R(D^{(*)})$, $b \rightarrow s \ell^+ \ell^-$ transitions and the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon. In this article, we lay the groundwork for further automated analyses by presenting the complete Lagrangian and the corresponding set of Feynman rules for scalar leptoquarks. This means we consider the five representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde1}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde2}$ and $\Phi_3$ and include the triple and quartic self-interactions, as well as couplings to the Standard Model (SM) fermions, gauge bosons and the Higgs. The calculations are performed using FeynRules and all model files are publicly available online at \url{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules}.
192: \end{abstract}

221: {\em Nature of problem:} In order to explain the deviations from SM predictions in $R(D^{(*)})$, $b \to \ell^+\ell^-$ transitions and the muon AMM jointly, models involving multiple LQ representations are necessary. This significantly increases the number of possible interactions and creates the need for computational tools that allow for studying the phenomenology of these LQ models in an automated manner. While model files exist for each LQ representation individually~[1], we are not aware of any publicly available model files that combine all scalar LQ representations as well as their self-interactions. \\
222: {\em Solution method:} We implemented the complete scalar LQ Lagrangian in a FeynRules~[2] model file and provide the corresponding MOD and UFO model files. These can be imported directly in FeynArts~[3] and MadGraph~[4] to obtain a versatile toolbox for the study of scalar LQs.  \\

242: \section{Introduction}
243: \label{sec:introduction}
244: 
245: Leptoquarks (LQs) are hypothetical beyond the Standard Model (BSM) particles that were first proposed in the context of Grand Unified Theories~\cite{Pati:1974yy, Georgi:1974sy, Georgi:1974yf, Fritzsch:1974nn}. What makes them stand out, and defines them, are their direct couplings to leptons and quarks (i.e. they convert a quark into a lepton and vice versa).  LQs were first systematically classified in Ref.~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs}, where ten possible LQ representations under the Standard Model (SM) gauge group were found, of which five are scalar (spin 0) and five are vector (spin 1) particles. While they have received varying degrees of attention since then, LQs have undergone a renaissance in recent years. This can be attributed to the emergence of observed flavor anomalies, i.e. the deviations from the SM predictions measured in several flavour observables. In particular,  $R(D^{(*)})$~\cite{Lees:2012xj,Lees:2013uzd,Aaij:2015yra,Aaij:2017deq,Aaij:2017uff,Abdesselam:2019dgh}, $b \rightarrow s \ell^+ \ell^-$ observables~\cite{CMS:2014xfa,Aaij:2015oid,Abdesselam:2016llu,Aaij:2017vbb,Aaij:2019wad,Aaij:2020nrf,Aaij:2021vac} and the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a_\mu$~\cite{Bennett:2006fi,Abi:2021gix} deviate from their SM predictions by $>3\sigma$~\cite{Amhis:2016xyh,Murgui:2019czp,Shi:2019gxi,Blanke:2019qrx,Kumbhakar:2019avh}, $>5\sigma$~\cite{Capdevila:2017bsm, Altmannshofer:2017yso,Alguero:2019ptt,Alok:2019ufo,Ciuchini:2019usw,Aebischer:2019mlg, Arbey:2019duh,Kumar:2019nfv} and $>4.2\sigma$~\cite{Aoyama:2020ynm}, respectively. Recently, the authors of Ref.~\cite{Bobeth:2021lya} unveiled a further $\approx 4 \sigma$ tension with the SM prediction in the forward-backward asymmetry of $\bar{B} \to D^{*} \ell \nu$. While these hints for new physics are by themselves interesting, it is intriguing to note that they all fall into a common pattern, namely lepton flavour universality violation.

249: Many models that are now being proposed to explain the flavour anomalies jointly contain multiple scalar leptoquark representations~\cite{Crivellin:2019dwb, Saad:2020ihm, Crivellin:2017zlb, Gherardi:2020qhc, Bigaran:2019bqv, Greljo:2021xmg, DaRold:2020bib, Babu:2020hun, Bigaran:2020jil, Gargalionis:2019drk, Saad:2020ucl, Chen:2016dip}. In addition to couplings of LQs to the SM fermions and gauge bosons, also interactions with the particles of the Higgs sector and between the LQs themselves are present in such a setup. In this article, we lay the groundwork for future automated LQ analyses by presenting the complete set of Feynman rules for all five scalar LQs. We include the $\text{LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs)}$, LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) and LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ couplings, as well as all couplings to the SM fermions and gauge bosons. The FeynRules~\cite{Alloul:2013bka} model files as well as the corresponding  MOD and UFO files are publicly available online at \url{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules} and can be used for automatized LQ phenomenology using FeynArts~\cite{Hahn:2000kx} or MadGraph~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}. \\
250: 
251: In Sections~\ref{sec:SMLagrangian} and \ref{sec:LQLagrangian}, we present our conventions by defining the complete Lagrangian for the SM extended with all five scalar LQ representations. Sec.~\ref{sec:methods} gives an overview on the computational tools and in Sec.~\ref{sec:SMInteractions}, the Feynman rules for the SM interactions are listed, while the ones for the scalar LQs are given in Sec.~\ref{sec:LQInteractions}. A detailed description of our treatment of charge-conjugate fermions can be found in~\ref{sec:appendix}.

261: \section{SM Lagrangian}
262: \label{sec:SMLagrangian}
263: The SM fermions and the Higgs field transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as
264: 
265: 
266: \begin{equation}
267: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
268:     \centering
269:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c c}
270:          & $Q^\prime_i$ & $u^\prime_i$ & $d^\prime_i$ & $L^\prime_i$ & $\ell^\prime_i$ & $H$\\ \hline
271:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\
272:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\
273:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $\frac{2}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{2}$ & -1 & $\frac{1}{2}$
274:     \end{tabular}\,.
275: \end{equation}
276: The prime indicates that these are the weak eigenstates. With this convention, the electric charge $Q$ can be calculated via the Gell-Mann-Nishijima formula
277: \begin{equation}
278: \label{eq:Gell-Mann-Nishijima}
279:     Q = I_3 + Y \,,
280: \end{equation}
281: 
282: 
283: where $Y$ is the $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge and $I_3$ the third component of the weak isospin. The left-handed quarks are components of the $SU(2)_L$-doublet $Q^\prime$ and the right-handed ones correspond to the singlets $u^\prime, d^\prime$
284: 
285: 
286: \begin{equation}
287:     Q^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
288:             u^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
289:             d^\prime_{i, L}
290:         \end{pmatrix}, 
291:     u^\prime_i = \left(u^\prime_{i, R}\right) \text{ and } 
292:     d^\prime_i = \left(d^\prime_{i, R}\right)\,,
293: \end{equation}
294: 
295: 
296: where $i = 1,2,3$ is the flavor index. Analogous conventions hold for the leptons
297: 
298: 
299: \begin{equation}
300:     L^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
301:             \nu^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
302:             \ell^\prime_{i, L}
303:         \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } 
304:     \ell^\prime_i = \left(\ell^\prime_{i, R}\right) \,.
305: \end{equation}
306: 
307: 
308: Note that right-handed neutrinos are not considered in this work. The SM Lagrangian then takes the form
309: 
310: 
311: \begin{align}
312:     \begin{aligned}
313:         \mathcal{L}^{\text{SM}}&= - \frac{1}{4} B^{\mu \nu} B_{\mu\nu} 
314:         - \frac{1}{4} W^{I, \mu \nu} W_{I, \mu\nu}
315:         - \frac{1}{4} G^{\alpha, \mu \nu} G_{\alpha, \mu\nu} \\
316:         &\phantom{12} + i \left(\bar{Q}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} Q_i^\prime\right)   + i \left(\bar{L}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} L_i^\prime\right)  + i \bar{u}_i^\prime \slashed{D} u_i^\prime  + i \bar{d}_i^\prime \slashed{D} d_i^\prime + i \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \slashed{D} \ell_i^\prime  \\
317:         &\phantom{12} +\left(\left(D^\mu H\right)^{\dagger} D_\mu H\right) + \mu_H^2 \left(H^\dagger H \right) - \lambda_H \left(H^\dagger H \right)^2 \\
318:         &\phantom{12} - \left(Y^d_{ij} \left(\bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) d^\prime_j 
319:         +Y^\ell_{ij} \left(\bar{L}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) \ell_j^\prime  
320:         + Y^u_{ij} \left( \bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i \tilde{H} \right) u_j^\prime + \text{ h.c.}\right) \\
321:         &\phantom{12} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}} \,.
322:         \label{eq:SM_lagrangian}
323:     \end{aligned}
324: \end{align}
325: We use brackets to indicate the $SU(2)_L$ contractions and denote the transpose of a $SU(2)_L$ multiplet $\Phi$ as $\Phi^\intercal$. $B^{\mu\nu}, W^{I, \mu \nu}$ (with $I \in \{1,2,3\}$) and $G^{\alpha, \mu \nu}$ (with $\alpha \in \{1, \dots ,8\}$) are the field strength tensors
326: \begin{equation}
327:     \begin{aligned}
328:     B_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu B_\nu - \partial_\nu B_\mu \,, \\
329:     W^{I}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu W^I_\nu - \partial_\nu W^I_\mu + g f^{IJK} W_\mu^J W_\nu^K \,, \\
330:     G^{\alpha}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu G^\alpha_\nu - \partial_\nu G^\alpha_\mu + g f^{\alpha \beta \gamma} W_\mu^\beta W_\nu^\gamma \,,
331:     \end{aligned}
332: \end{equation} 
333: 
334: 
335: where $B_\mu, W^I_\mu, G^\alpha_\mu$ are the gauge fields corresponding to $U(1)_{Y}$, $SU(2)_{L}$ and $SU(3)_{c}$, respectively. $f^{IJK}$, $f^{\alpha \beta \gamma}$ denote the structure constants of $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$. $Y^d$, $Y^\ell$, $Y^u$ are the Yukawa couplings and $\tilde{H} \equiv i\sigma_2 H^\dagger$, where $\sigma_2$ is the second Pauli matrix. In our conventions, the Pauli matrices are given by
336: 
337: 
338: \begin{equation}
339: \sigma_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \, \sigma_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} ,\, \sigma_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}\,.
340: \end{equation}
341: 
342: 
343: The covariant derivative is defined as
344: 
345: 
346: \begin{equation}
347: D_\mu \phi = \partial_\mu \phi - ig_1 Y B_\mu \phi - ig_2  \tau_{I} W^{I}_\mu \phi - ig_s T_{\alpha} G^{\alpha}_\mu \phi \,,
348: \end{equation}
349: 
350: 
351: with $I \in \{ 1,2,3 \}$, $\alpha \in \{1, \dots, 8\}$. $\tau_{I} = \frac{\sigma_I}{2}, T_{\alpha} = \frac{\lambda_\alpha}{2}$ refer to the generators of the fundamental $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$ representations here. The gauge-fixing part $\mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}}$ of the Lagrangian is described in Eq.~(\ref{eq:gaugefixing}). \\
352: 
353: Having acquired a non-zero vacuum expectation value (VEV) $v \approx 246$ GeV after spontaneous symmetry breaking, the Higgs doublet $H$ can be expanded in modes around $v$
354: 
355: 
356: \begin{equation}
357: H = \begin{pmatrix}
358: -i\varphi^+ \\
359: \frac{v + h + i\varphi_Z}{\sqrt{2}}\\
360: \end{pmatrix}\,,
361: \end{equation}
362: 
363: 
364: where $\varphi^+$ and $\varphi_Z$ are the Goldstone bosons and $h$ the physical Higgs field with $m_h \approx $ \SI{125}{\giga \electronvolt}. Expressed in terms of the couplings $\mu_H, \lambda_H$ (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:SM_lagrangian})), the parameters $v, m_h$ read
365: 
366: 
367: \begin{equation}
368:     \begin{aligned}
369:     m_h &= \sqrt{2} \mu_H \,, \\
370:     v &= \dfrac{\mu_H}{\sqrt{\lambda_H}} \,. 
371:     \end{aligned}
372: \end{equation}
373: 
374: 
375: The non-vanishing VEV leads to mixing of the $U(1)_Y$ gauge boson with the neutral component of the $SU(2)_L$ ones
376: 
377: 
378: \begin{align}
379:     \begin{aligned}
380:         \begin{pmatrix}
381:             A_\mu\\ 
382:             Z_\mu
383:         \end{pmatrix} &= 
384:         \begin{pmatrix}
385:             \cos \theta_w & \sin \theta_w \\
386:             -\sin \theta_w & \cos \theta_w
387:         \end{pmatrix}
388:                 \begin{pmatrix}
389:             B_\mu\\ 
390:             W^3_\mu
391:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
392:      \end{aligned}
393:      \label{eq:EWMixing1}
394: \end{align}
395: 
396: 
397: where $\theta_w$ is the Weinberg angle. The remaining two $SU(2)_L$ gauge bosons form electric charge eigenstates
398: 
399: 
400: \begin{align}
401:     \begin{aligned}
402:         W^\pm_\mu &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left( W^1_\mu \mp i W^2_\mu \right) \,. \label{eq:EWMixing2}
403:         \end{aligned}
404: \end{align}
405: 
406: 
407: In the following, $\cos \theta_w, \sin \theta_w$ will be abbreviated as $c_w, s_w$. Instead of using the coupling constants $g_1, g_2$ directly, we will state the Feynman rules using the electric charge $e$. The conversion back to $g_1, g_2$ is easily carried out using 
408: 
409: 
410: \begin{align}
411:     \begin{aligned}
412:         e = c_w   g_1 \,, \\
413:         e = s_w   g_2\,.
414:     \end{aligned}
415: \end{align}
416: 
417: 
418: The masses acquired by the gauge bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{eq:EWMixing1}) and (\ref{eq:EWMixing2}) via spontaneous symmetry breaking are
419: 
420: 
421: \begin{equation}
422:     \begin{aligned}
423:         m_A &= 0 \,, \\
424:         m_W &= \frac{v}{2}\frac{e}{s_w} \,, \\
425:         m_Z &= \frac{v}{2}\frac{e}{s_w c_w} \,,
426:     \end{aligned}
427:     \label{eq:bosonMasses}
428: \end{equation}
429: 
430: 
431: from which it becomes clear that $A_\mu$ corresponds to the photon. As stated above, $Y^d, Y^u, Y^\ell$ denote the Yukawa couplings of the Higgs doublet for the down-type quarks, up-type quarks and leptons, respectively. After spontaneous symmetry breaking, they yield non-diagonal mass terms in the weak basis
432: 
433: 
434: \begin{equation}
435:     \begin{aligned}
436:         m^u_{ij} \bar{u}_i^\prime u_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^u_{ij}\ \bar{u}^\prime_{i} u^\prime_{j}\,, \\
437:         m^d_{ij} \bar{d}_i^\prime d_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^d_{ij}\ \bar{d}^\prime_{i} d^\prime_{j}\,, \\
438:         m^\ell_{ij} \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \ell_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^\ell_{ij}\ \bar{\ell}^\prime_{i} \ell^\prime_{j}\,. 
439:     \end{aligned}
440: \end{equation}
441: 
442: 
443: These can be diagonalized by rotating the fermion fields
444: 
445: 
446: \begin{equation}
447: \begin{aligned}
448: u_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{uL}_{ij} u_{j, L} \,, & u_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{uR}_{ij} u_{j, R}   \,, \\
449: d_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{dL}_{ij} d_{j, L} \,, & d_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{dR}_{ij} d_{j, R}  \,, \\
450: \ell_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell L}_{ij} \ell_{j, L}  \,, & \ell_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell R}_{ij} \ell_{j, R}\,,
451: \end{aligned}
452: \label{eq:fermionRotation}
453: \end{equation}
454: 
455:

457: \begin{equation}

461:     \hat{Y}^\ell &\equiv \left(U^{\ell L}\right)^\dagger Y^\ell U^{\ell R} \,,\\

467: are diagonal and are related to the fermion masses by

474:     \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{Y}^\ell &= \text{diag}(m_{\ell_1}, m_{\ell_2},m_{\ell_3}) \,.\\

480: The unitary matrices in Eq.~(\ref{eq:fermionRotation}) can for the most part be absorbed into redefinitions of the fermion fields, the only remaining physical matrix being in the weak charged current for quarks, the CKM matrix $V$

483: \begin{equation}
484: \begin{aligned}
485:     \mathcal{L}^{SM} &\supset \frac{e}{\sqrt{2} s_w} W_\mu^+ \bar{u}^\prime_{i,L} \gamma^\mu d^\prime_{i,L} + \text{ h.c.} \\
486:     &= \frac{e}{\sqrt{2} s_w} W_\mu^+ \bar{u}_{k,L} \gamma^\mu \underbrace{\left(U^{uL} \right)_{ki}^\dagger \left(U^{dL}\right)_{il}}_{V_{kl}} d_{l,L} + \text{ h.c.} \,.
487: \end{aligned}

491: Without loss of generality, we can therefore assume that the relations between the weak eigenstates $u^\prime, d^\prime, \ell^\prime, \nu^\prime$ and the mass eigenstates $u,d, \ell, \nu$ take the form

494: \begin{equation}
495:     \begin{aligned}
496:         u^\prime_{i, L} &= u_{i, L} \,, &u^\prime_{i, R} &= u_{i, R} \,, \\
497:         d^\prime_{i, L} &= V_{ij} d_{j, L} \,, &d^\prime_{i, R} &= d_{i, R} \,, \\
498:         \ell^\prime_{i, L} &= \ell_{i, L} \,, &\ell^\prime_{i, R} &= \ell_{i, R} \,, \\
499:         \nu^\prime_{i, L} &= \nu_{i, L} \,, & &
500:     \end{aligned}

505: meaning that CKM elements only appear in couplings involving left-handed down-type quarks (corresponding to the up basis). Note that while this choice does not affect the SM Feynman rules, it becomes relevant in LQ interactions with SM fermions. The gauge freedoms of the SM gauge bosons are given in Ref.~\cite{Romao:2012pq} (our conventions correspond to $\eta_Y, \eta_Z, \eta_\theta, \eta_G = 1$ and $\eta, \eta_s, \eta_e, \eta^\prime = -1$). They are fixed using the Fadeev-Popov prescription~\cite{Faddeev:1967fc}. Working in the Feynman gauge, we add the following gauge-fixing terms, after spontaneous symmetry breaking and expressed in terms of the physical fields $A_\mu, Z_\mu, W_\mu^\pm, G_\mu^\alpha$ and their corresponding ghost fields $c_A, c_Z, c_{W^\pm}, c_{G^\alpha}$, to the Lagrangian

511:  &\phantom{12} - \left(\partial^\mu W_\mu^- + i m_W \varphi^- \right)\left(\partial^\mu W_\mu^+ - i m_W \varphi^+ \right) \\
512:  &\phantom{12}- \frac{1}{2}\left(\partial^\mu G_\mu^\alpha \right)^2 \\
513: &\phantom{12} +\sum_{B \in \{A,Z,W^\pm \}} \bigg( \bar{c}_{W^+} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{W^+})}{\partial \alpha_B} + \bar{c}_{W^-} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{W^+})}{\partial \alpha_B}  \\
514: &\phantom{12 + \sum_{B \in \{A,Z,W^\pm \}}}+ \bar{c}_Z \frac{\partial(\delta F_Z)}{\partial \alpha_B} + \bar{c}_A \frac{\partial(\delta F_A)}{\partial \alpha_B}\bigg)c_B \\
515: &\phantom{12} + \sum_{\alpha, \beta = 1}^{8} \bar{c}_{G^\alpha} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{G^\alpha})}{\partial \alpha_{G^\beta}} c_{G^\beta}\,.
516:  \end{aligned}

539: \section{LQ Lagrangian}
540: \label{sec:LQLagrangian}
541: The five possible scalar LQ representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde{1}}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde{2}}, \Phi_3$ transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs} 
542: 
543: 
544: \begin{equation}
545: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
546:     \centering
547:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c}
548:          & $\Phi_1,$ & $\Phi_{\tilde{1}}$ & $\Phi_2$ & $ \Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ & $\Phi_3$\\ \hline
549:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\
550:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\
551:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$ & $-\frac{4}{3}$ & $\frac{7}{6}$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$
552:     \end{tabular}\,.
553: \end{equation}
554: 
555: 
556: Note that we adopt the convention that all scalar LQs transform in the fundamental $SU(3)_c$ representation. Expanding the $SU(2)_L$ multiplets into their components, the following electric charge eigenstates are found
557: 
558: 
559: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
560: \begin{align}
561:     \begin{aligned}
562:         \Phi_1 = \left( \Phi_1^{-1/3}\right), \ 
563:         \Phi_{\tilde{1}} = \left( \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3}\right), \ 
564:         \Phi_2 = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+5/3}_2 \\ \Phi^{+2/3}_2 \end{pmatrix},\ \\
565:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
566:         \Phi_{\tilde{2}} = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\ \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \end{pmatrix},\ 
567:         \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3} = \begin{pmatrix}
568:             \Phi_3^{-1/3} & \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{+2/3} \\
569:             \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{-4/3} & -\Phi_3^{-1/3}
570:         \end{pmatrix}\,. 
571:     \end{aligned}
572: \end{align}
573: 
574: 
575: We decompose the scalar LQ Lagrangian as
576: 
577: 
578: \begin{equation}
579:     \mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}} = \mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} +
580:     \mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}  + \mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi} \,,
581: \end{equation}
582: 
583: 
584: where $\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$ contains the LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) couplings, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$  the kinetic terms and the couplings to the SM gauge bosons, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}$ the couplings to the SM fermions, $\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) couplings and finally $\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interaction terms. The individual parts of the Lagrangians are discussed in more detail below.

588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\
600:         &- iY_{33} \epsilon^{IJK} \left(H^\dagger \sigma^I H \right) \Phi_3^{J\dagger} \Phi_3^K\\
601:          \Big[&- A_{1\tilde{2}}\big( \Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger H \big)\Phi_1 + A_{\tilde{2}3}\big(\Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger \left(\sigma \cdot \Phi_3\right) H \big) + Y_{2\tilde{2}}\big(\Phi_{2}^\dagger H \big)\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\Phi_{\tilde{2}}\big)\\
602:         &+Y_{\tilde{1}3}\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3}\right)^\dagger H\big)\Phi_{\tilde{1}} + Y_{13} \big(H^{\dagger}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3} \right)H \big)\Phi_{1}^{\dagger} + \text{h.c.}\Big] \,.
603:     \end{aligned}
604:     \label{eq:LQ_mixing}
605: \end{equation}
606: 
607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\

1107: \subsection{Quartic LQ Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$)}
1108: To get four-LQ interaction terms in the Lagrangian, one needs to combine two LQs and two anti-LQs, since
1109: 
1110: 
1111: \begin{equation}
1112: 3 \otimes \overline{3} \otimes 3 \otimes \overline{3} = 1 \oplus 1 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 10 \oplus \overline{10} \oplus 27
1113: \label{eq:SU(3)_singlets}
1114: \end{equation}
1115: is the only tensor product of four $SU(3)_{c}$ fundamental representations $\left(3, \overline{3}\right)$ that contains a singlet. Trivial combinations of LQ fields that contribute to the four-LQ Lagrangian are of the type
1116: \begin{equation}
1117: \begin{aligned}
1118: Y^{(1)}_{a} \left(\Phi^\dagger_{a, c_1} \Phi_{a, c_1}\right) \left( \Phi^\dagger_{a, c_2} \Phi_{a, c_2} \right)\,, \\
1119: Y^{(1)}_{ab} \left(\Phi^\dagger_{a, c_1} \Phi_{a, c_1}\right) \left( \Phi^\dagger_{b, c_2} \Phi_{b, c_2} \right)\,,
1120: \end{aligned}
1121: \label{eq:obviouscombination}
1122: \end{equation}
1123: 
1124: 
1125: where $a \neq b \in \left\{1,\tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right\}$. All additional combinations that result in a vanishing total weak hypercharge $Y$ are given in Tab.~\ref{tab:quartic}.

1202: \section{Methods}
1203: \label{sec:methods}
1204: 
1205: The determination of the Feynman rules to be presented in Chapters \ref{sec:SMInteractions} and \ref{sec:LQInteractions} is carried out using the Mathematica package FeynRules 2.3.36~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}. All model files and the Mathematica notebook needed to display and export the Feynman rules can be found online at GitLab. In the following, the structure of the code files will be discussed. For more information about FeynRules, the interested reader is referred to Ref.~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}.

2596: \section{Scalar LQ Feynman Rules}
2597: \label{sec:LQInteractions}
2598: In this section we state the Feynman rules for all LQ interactions. We write $\Phi^q_a$ with $q \in \{-\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3},+\frac{5}{3} \}$ and $a \in \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3\}$. For $q = +\frac{5}{3}$, $\hat{\Phi}^{+5/3}$ is just a single field, therefore the subscript $a$ is omitted. The LQ electric charge eigenstate vectors are given in Eq.~(\ref{eq:ChargeVectors}).

2662: \subsection{Interactions with SM Fermions}
2663: \label{sec:LQfermions}
2664: The Feynman rules for LQ interactions with the SM fermions are given below. All fields are defined to be incoming. We omit the color indices whenever they just involve trivial contractions. We express some of the rules using $n_a^q$, which is defined in Eq.~(\ref{eq:nqi}). Whenever $q$ is clear from the context, we write $n_a^q$ as $n_a$ to simplify the notation. The bar labels an antifermion. Note that while there is an equivalence between a fermion field $f$ and $\bar{f}^c$, stating Feynman rules for $\bar{f}^c$ makes sense in our treatment of charge-conjugate fermions. A detailed explanation is given in~\ref{sec:appendix}.

display.text:
You are benchmarking automated extraction of a BSM physics model from its paper, to be compared against the physicist's own FeynRules implementation.

MODEL: SLQrules (SimpleExtensions) — FeynRules DB entry based on arXiv:2105.04844.
PAPER: the paper's LaTeX source is the file "paper/2105.04844_source.tex" (read it completely with your file-reading tool; equations, fractions and roots are exact; it is authoritative).
SCHEMA: read tools/frgen/frmodel.py (pydantic FeynRulesModel) before you write the spec.

TASK — extract the COMPLETE new-physics content:
1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — a model with several new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) must include all of them as separate ParticleClass entries (or class_members).
2. Identify the new coupling/mass/mixing parameters (External unless clearly derived).
3. Include the main new-physics lagrangian_terms (verbatim Mathematica strings, FeynRules idioms).

SCHEMA RULES: all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on => gauge_groups []; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need NO declaration; any OTHER index (e.g. a colour-sextet index, a new-generation index) NEEDS an index_decls entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique class_index; self_conjugate=false for complex fields (distinct antiparticle), true for real/Majorana fields.

OUTPUT: write the FeynRulesModel JSON object to spec.json in the current directory with your file-writing tool (ONLY the JSON). Set model_name to "SLQrules_gen". Run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate as described under TOOLKIT. Your final message: the self-audit table and one line with the last ./frgen result. spec.json as it is on disk when you stop is rendered and scored.

SANDBOX: the current directory contains ONLY the paper (paper/2105.04844_source.tex), SM.fr (the Standard
Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer
tools/frgen/render.py, the lints tools/fr_lint.py and the command ./frgen. Nothing else
exists here and nothing outside this directory may be read. You have file read, search and
write tools, and ONE shell command: `./frgen spec.json`. No other shell command, no web,
no FeynRules, no Mathematica and no MadGraph.

TOOLKIT: `./frgen spec.json` (1) validates spec.json against the FeynRulesModel schema and
prints every schema error, (2) renders model.fr with the deterministic renderer, and (3)
lints model.fr with deterministic rules, each tagged with the stage it predicts will fail.
Run it after you write spec.json, fix what it reports, and run it again until the schema
is OK and every remaining lint finding is one you have checked and judged harmless.

AUTOMATIC CHECK: after every write or edit of spec.json the toolkit runs by itself and
its report is appended to that tool's result. Read it after each change and fix what it
reports. You may still run `./frgen spec.json` yourself.

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
   Never silently pick one placement.

8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.

## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)

9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Write covariant derivatives on the whole field, `DC[Phi, mu]`, never with an explicit colour index inside `DC[...]`.

10. Names. Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). No primes or punctuation in `ParticleName`/`AntiParticleName` (`W'` is not a valid UFO name; write `Wp`, `Wpbar`). Use class indices of 100 or more for new classes.

11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. Declare `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` with every order you use (for example `{{QCD, 1}, {QED, 2}, {NP, 1}}`). A coupling with no order makes MadGraph reject the UFO ("Some couplings have '1' order").

12. Tensor parameters. Give every indexed parameter explicit per-component values (`yN[1,1] -> 0.1, yN[1,2] -> 0, ...`; schema: `value_rules`). Never use a pattern rule such as `X[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> ...` in `Definitions`: FeynRules exports the pattern verbatim as a UFO parameter name and MadGraph fails with an unrelated "invalid syntax" error.

13. Flavour structure in matrix form. Write generation-space couplings as matrix products between class fields, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS`, not as explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[ff1, cc]...dq[ff2, cc]`, and never nest one generation index inside another. Explicit-index forms leak FeynRules internals (`ConvertSpinToString`, `MakeIdenticalFermions`) into the UFO.

14. One declared total. Define exactly one Lagrangian term named `LTotal` that sums every other term you define, and make sure every other term appears in that sum. Do not define two alternative totals. Do not emit a term that contains no field (a pure constant): FeynRules exports it as a vertex with no particles.

15. Declarations. Every field used in a term is declared; every parameter used in a term is declared with a numeric default; every `SelfConjugate -> True` class has no `QuantumNumbers`; a Majorana mass term is `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.

## Mandatory self-audit table (produce it BEFORE the model)

For every Lagrangian term you emit, output one row of this table. Then fix any row that fails before you write the model.

| term name | fields in the monomial | operator mass dimension d | coupling symbol | coupling mass dimension (must be 4 - d) | 1/Lambda power present (must be d - 4, or "n/a" if d <= 4) | Q sum | Y sum | SU(2) contraction (singlet? which Eps or shared index) | SU(3) contraction | sum of each new U(1) charge (one column per U(1), must be 0) | lepton/baryon number sum (if the paper assigns them) | CC[] used where paper writes psi^c (yes/no/n/a) | fraction/root placement checked against (equation, LaTeX line, or "n/a") | Hermitian partner (HC[] or self-conjugate) |

Rules for the table:
- Field mass dimensions: scalar 1, vector 1, fermion 3/2, `FS[...]` 2, `del`/`DC` 1.
- Every Q sum, Y sum, and new-U(1) sum must equal 0. Use the charges you declared in `QuantumNumbers` and the SM.fr charges for SM fields. If a sum is not 0, the term is wrong; fix the contraction or the charge before you continue.
- If d > 4, the row must show `1/Lambda^(d-4)` and an External cutoff parameter, or a Description that states the absorbed dimension and units.
- Add one row per new particle class that confirms its kinetic + mass term exists and is in the total Lagrangian sum.
- Add one row per non-fundamental colour representation that confirms the `AddGaugeRepresentation[...]` line is present.
- Add one line under the table that lists every `SelfConjugate -> True` class and confirms it carries no `QuantumNumbers`.
- Add one line that lists every class, parameter and index name you chose and confirms none is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol, or an SM.fr name.
- Add one line that names the single total Lagrangian and lists the terms it sums.
- Add one line that states whether any reference or cached model file was read (must be "none").

384: def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
385:     """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
386:     if not text:
387:         return False

391: def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
392:     """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
393:     texts: List[str] = []
394:     if p.value:
395:         texts.append(p.value)

398:     for r in p.definitions:

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )
433:     return ordered

436: _INDEX_SIZE = {"Generation": 3, "Colour": 3, "Gluon": 8, "SU2D": 2, "SU2W": 3}

439: def _block_entries(p: Parameter, sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> set:
440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""
441:     if not p.is_tensor:
442:         return {(p.order_block,)} if p.order_block is not None else set()

444:     for r in p.value_rules:
445:         m = re.fullmatch(rf"\s*{re.escape(p.name)}\s*\[([0-9,\s]+)\]\s*", r.lhs)
446:         if m:
447:             entries.add(tuple(int(x) for x in m.group(1).split(",")))
448:     if entries:
449:         return entries
450:     ranges = [range(1, sizes.get(i, 3) + 1) for i in p.indices]
451:     out = {()}
452:     for rg in ranges:
453:         out = {e + (k,) for e in out for k in rg}
454:     return out

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:
458:     """External parameters that share an LHA block must not share an entry.
459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO
462:     with one name defined twice, and MadGraph rejects the model ("name VLq1x1
463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():
471:         owner: Dict[tuple, str] = {}

473:             for e in sorted(_block_entries(p, sizes)):
474:                 if e in owner and owner[e] != p.name:
475:                     raise ValueError(
476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )
481:                 owner[e] = p.name

77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0

82:             i += 2

96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0

99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

316:     if model.interaction_order_limit:

318:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
319:     if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
320:         sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
321:     if model.vevs:
322:         vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
323:         sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")

325:     for raw in model.raw_preamble:

328:     if model.index_decls:

330:     if model.gauge_groups:

332:     if model.parameters:

334:         # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
335:         # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
336:         # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
337:         reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338:         params = [p for p in model.parameters
339:                   if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
340:         if params:
341:             sections.append(render_parameters(params))
342:     if model.particles:
343:         sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
344:     for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345:         sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346: 
347:     for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348:         sections.append(raw)
349: 
350:     for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351:         op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352:         # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353:         # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354:         # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355:         rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356:         for lead in (":=", "="):
357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361: 
362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365:         keep_trailing_newline=True,
366:     )
367:     template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368:     return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))

242: \section{Introduction}
243: \label{sec:introduction}
244: 
245: Leptoquarks (LQs) are hypothetical beyond the Standard Model (BSM) particles that were first proposed in the context of Grand Unified Theories~\cite{Pati:1974yy, Georgi:1974sy, Georgi:1974yf, Fritzsch:1974nn}. What makes them stand out, and defines them, are their direct couplings to leptons and quarks (i.e. they convert a quark into a lepton and vice versa).  LQs were first systematically classified in Ref.~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs}, where ten possible LQ representations under the Standard Model (SM) gauge group were found, of which five are scalar (spin 0) and five are vector (spin 1) particles. While they have received varying degrees of attention since then, LQs have undergone a renaissance in recent years. This can be attributed to the emergence of observed flavor anomalies, i.e. the deviations from the SM predictions measured in several flavour observables. In particular,  $R(D^{(*)})$~\cite{Lees:2012xj,Lees:2013uzd,Aaij:2015yra,Aaij:2017deq,Aaij:2017uff,Abdesselam:2019dgh}, $b \rightarrow s \ell^+ \ell^-$ observables~\cite{CMS:2014xfa,Aaij:2015oid,Abdesselam:2016llu,Aaij:2017vbb,Aaij:2019wad,Aaij:2020nrf,Aaij:2021vac} and the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a_\mu$~\cite{Bennett:2006fi,Abi:2021gix} deviate from their SM predictions by $>3\sigma$~\cite{Amhis:2016xyh,Murgui:2019czp,Shi:2019gxi,Blanke:2019qrx,Kumbhakar:2019avh}, $>5\sigma$~\cite{Capdevila:2017bsm, Altmannshofer:2017yso,Alguero:2019ptt,Alok:2019ufo,Ciuchini:2019usw,Aebischer:2019mlg, Arbey:2019duh,Kumar:2019nfv} and $>4.2\sigma$~\cite{Aoyama:2020ynm}, respectively. Recently, the authors of Ref.~\cite{Bobeth:2021lya} unveiled a further $\approx 4 \sigma$ tension with the SM prediction in the forward-backward asymmetry of $\bar{B} \to D^{*} \ell \nu$. While these hints for new physics are by themselves interesting, it is intriguing to note that they all fall into a common pattern, namely lepton flavour universality violation.

249: Many models that are now being proposed to explain the flavour anomalies jointly contain multiple scalar leptoquark representations~\cite{Crivellin:2019dwb, Saad:2020ihm, Crivellin:2017zlb, Gherardi:2020qhc, Bigaran:2019bqv, Greljo:2021xmg, DaRold:2020bib, Babu:2020hun, Bigaran:2020jil, Gargalionis:2019drk, Saad:2020ucl, Chen:2016dip}. A detailed description of our treatment of charge-conjugate fermions can be found in~\ref{sec:appendix}.

261: \section{SM Lagrangian}
262: \label{sec:SMLagrangian}
263: The SM fermions and the Higgs field transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as
264: 
265: 
266: \begin{equation}
267: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
268:     \centering
269:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c c}
270:          & $Q^\prime_i$ & $u^\prime_i$ & $d^\prime_i$ & $L^\prime_i$ & $\ell^\prime_i$ & $H$\\ \hline
271:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\
272:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\
273:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $\frac{2}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{2}$ & -1 & $\frac{1}{2}$
274:     \end{tabular}\,.
275: \end{equation}
276: The prime indicates that these are the weak eigenstates. With this convention, the electric charge $Q$ can be calculated via the Gell-Mann-Nishijima formula
277: \begin{equation}
278: \label{eq:Gell-Mann-Nishijima}
279:     Q = I_3 + Y \,,
280: \end{equation}
281: 
282: 
283: where $Y$ is the $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge and $I_3$ the third component of the weak isospin. The left-handed quarks are components of the $SU(2)_L$-doublet $Q^\prime$ and the right-handed ones correspond to the singlets $u^\prime, d^\prime$
284: 
285: 
286: \begin{equation}
287:     Q^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
288:             u^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
289:             d^\prime_{i, L}
290:         \end{pmatrix}, 
291:     u^\prime_i = \left(u^\prime_{i, R}\right) \text{ and } 
292:     d^\prime_i = \left(d^\prime_{i, R}\right)\,,
293: \end{equation}
294: 
295: 
296: where $i = 1,2,3$ is the flavor index. Analogous conventions hold for the leptons
297: 
298: 
299: \begin{equation}
300:     L^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
301:             \nu^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
302:             \ell^\prime_{i, L}
303:         \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } 
304:     \ell^\prime_i = \left(\ell^\prime_{i, R}\right) \,.
305: \end{equation}
306: 
307: 
308: Note that right-handed neutrinos are not considered in this work. The SM Lagrangian then takes the form
309: 
310: 
311: \begin{align}
312:     \begin{aligned}
313:         \mathcal{L}^{\text{SM}}&= - \frac{1}{4} B^{\mu \nu} B_{\mu\nu} 
314:         - \frac{1}{4} W^{I, \mu \nu} W_{I, \mu\nu}
315:         - \frac{1}{4} G^{\alpha, \mu \nu} G_{\alpha, \mu\nu} \\
316:         &\phantom{12} + i \left(\bar{Q}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} Q_i^\prime\right)   + i \left(\bar{L}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} L_i^\prime\right)  + i \bar{u}_i^\prime \slashed{D} u_i^\prime  + i \bar{d}_i^\prime \slashed{D} d_i^\prime + i \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \slashed{D} \ell_i^\prime  \\
317:         &\phantom{12} +\left(\left(D^\mu H\right)^{\dagger} D_\mu H\right) + \mu_H^2 \left(H^\dagger H \right) - \lambda_H \left(H^\dagger H \right)^2 \\
318:         &\phantom{12} - \left(Y^d_{ij} \left(\bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) d^\prime_j 
319:         +Y^\ell_{ij} \left(\bar{L}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) \ell_j^\prime  
320:         + Y^u_{ij} \left( \bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i \tilde{H} \right) u_j^\prime + \text{ h.c.}\right) \\
321:         &\phantom{12} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}} \,.
322:         \label{eq:SM_lagrangian}
323:     \end{aligned}
324: \end{align}
325: We use brackets to indicate the $SU(2)_L$ contractions and denote the transpose of a $SU(2)_L$ multiplet $\Phi$ as $\Phi^\intercal$. $B^{\mu\nu}, W^{I, \mu \nu}$ (with $I \in \{1,2,3\}$) and $G^{\alpha, \mu \nu}$ (with $\alpha \in \{1, \dots ,8\}$) are the field strength tensors
326: \begin{equation}
327:     \begin{aligned}
328:     B_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu B_\nu - \partial_\nu B_\mu \,, \\
329:     W^{I}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu W^I_\nu - \partial_\nu W^I_\mu + g f^{IJK} W_\mu^J W_\nu^K \,, \\
330:     G^{\alpha}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu G^\alpha_\nu - \partial_\nu G^\alpha_\mu + g f^{\alpha \beta \gamma} W_\mu^\beta W_\nu^\gamma \,,
331:     \end{aligned}
332: \end{equation} 
333: 
334: 
335: where $B_\mu, W^I_\mu, G^\alpha_\mu$ are the gauge fields corresponding to $U(1)_{Y}$, $SU(2)_{L}$ and $SU(3)_{c}$, respectively. $f^{IJK}$, $f^{\alpha \beta \gamma}$ denote the structure constants of $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$. $Y^d$, $Y^\ell$, $Y^u$ are the Yukawa couplings and $\tilde{H} \equiv i\sigma_2 H^\dagger$, where $\sigma_2$ is the second Pauli matrix. In our conventions, the Pauli matrices are given by
336: 
337: 
338: \begin{equation}
339: \sigma_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \, \sigma_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} ,\, \sigma_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}\,.
340: \end{equation}
341: 
342: 
343: The covariant derivative is defined as
344: 
345: 
346: \begin{equation}
347: D_\mu \phi = \partial_\mu \phi - ig_1 Y B_\mu \phi - ig_2  \tau_{I} W^{I}_\mu \phi - ig_s T_{\alpha} G^{\alpha}_\mu \phi \,,
348: \end{equation}
349: 
350: 
351: with $I \in \{ 1,2,3 \}$, $\alpha \in \{1, \dots, 8\}$. $\tau_{I} = \frac{\sigma_I}{2}, T_{\alpha} = \frac{\lambda_\alpha}{2}$ refer to the generators of the fundamental $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$ representations here. The gauge-fixing part $\mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}}$ of the Lagrangian is described in Eq.~(\ref{eq:gaugefixing}). \\
352: 
353: Having acquired a non-zero vacuum expectation value (VEV) $v \approx 246$ GeV after spontaneous symmetry breaking, the Higgs doublet $H$ can be expanded in modes around $v$
354: 
355: 
356: \begin{equation}
357: H = \begin{pmatrix}
358: -i\varphi^+ \\
359: \frac{v + h + i\varphi_Z}{\sqrt{2}}\\
360: \end{pmatrix}\,,
361: \end{equation}
362: 
363: 
364: where $\varphi^+$ and $\varphi_Z$ are the Goldstone bosons and $h$ the physical Higgs field with $m_h \approx $ \SI{125}{\giga \electronvolt}. Expressed in terms of the couplings $\mu_H, \lambda_H$ (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:SM_lagrangian})), the parameters $v, m_h$ read
365: 
366: 
367: \begin{equation}
368:     \begin{aligned}
369:     m_h &= \sqrt{2} \mu_H \,, \\
370:     v &= \dfrac{\mu_H}{\sqrt{\lambda_H}} \,. 
371:     \end{aligned}
372: \end{equation}
373: 
374: 
375: The non-vanishing VEV leads to mixing of the $U(1)_Y$ gauge boson with the neutral component of the $SU(2)_L$ ones
376: 
377: 
378: \begin{align}
379:     \begin{aligned}
380:         \begin{pmatrix}
381:             A_\mu\\ 
382:             Z_\mu
383:         \end{pmatrix} &= 
384:         \begin{pmatrix}
385:             \cos \theta_w & \sin \theta_w \\
386:             -\sin \theta_w & \cos \theta_w
387:         \end{pmatrix}
388:                 \begin{pmatrix}
389:             B_\mu\\ 
390:             W^3_\mu
391:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
392:      \end{aligned}
393:      \label{eq:EWMixing1}
394: \end{align}
395: 
396: 
397: where $\theta_w$ is the Weinberg angle. The remaining two $SU(2)_L$ gauge bosons form electric charge eigenstates
398:

418: The masses acquired by the gauge bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{eq:EWMixing1}) and (\ref{eq:EWMixing2}) via spontaneous symmetry breaking are

422:     \begin{aligned}

431: from which it becomes clear that $A_\mu$ corresponds to the photon. As stated above, $Y^d, Y^u, Y^\ell$ denote the Yukawa couplings of the Higgs doublet for the down-type quarks, up-type quarks and leptons, respectively. After spontaneous symmetry breaking, they yield non-diagonal mass terms in the weak basis
432: 
433: 
434: \begin{equation}
435:     \begin{aligned}
436:         m^u_{ij} \bar{u}_i^\prime u_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^u_{ij}\ \bar{u}^\prime_{i} u^\prime_{j}\,, \\

438:         m^\ell_{ij} \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \ell_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^\ell_{ij}\ \bar{\ell}^\prime_{i} \ell^\prime_{j}\,. 
439:     \end{aligned}
440: \end{equation}

442: 
443: These can be diagonalized by rotating the fermion fields
444: 
445: 
446: \begin{equation}
447: \begin{aligned}
448: u_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{uL}_{ij} u_{j, L} \,, & u_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{uR}_{ij} u_{j, R}   \,, \\
449: d_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{dL}_{ij} d_{j, L} \,, & d_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{dR}_{ij} d_{j, R}  \,, \\
450: \ell_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell L}_{ij} \ell_{j, L}  \,, & \ell_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell R}_{ij} \ell_{j, R}\,,
451: \end{aligned}

458:     \begin{aligned}
459:     \hat{Y}^u &\equiv \left(U^{uL}\right)^\dagger Y^u U^{uR} \,, \\

461:     \hat{Y}^\ell &\equiv \left(U^{\ell L}\right)^\dagger Y^\ell U^{\ell R} \,,\\

539: \section{LQ Lagrangian}
540: \label{sec:LQLagrangian}
541: The five possible scalar LQ representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde{1}}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde{2}}, \Phi_3$ transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs} 
542: 
543: 
544: \begin{equation}
545: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
546:     \centering
547:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c}
548:          & $\Phi_1,$ & $\Phi_{\tilde{1}}$ & $\Phi_2$ & $ \Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ & $\Phi_3$\\ \hline
549:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\
550:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\
551:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$ & $-\frac{4}{3}$ & $\frac{7}{6}$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$
552:     \end{tabular}\,.
553: \end{equation}
554: 
555: 
556: Note that we adopt the convention that all scalar LQs transform in the fundamental $SU(3)_c$ representation. Expanding the $SU(2)_L$ multiplets into their components, the following electric charge eigenstates are found
557: 
558: 
559: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
560: \begin{align}
561:     \begin{aligned}
562:         \Phi_1 = \left( \Phi_1^{-1/3}\right), \ 
563:         \Phi_{\tilde{1}} = \left( \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3}\right), \ 
564:         \Phi_2 = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+5/3}_2 \\ \Phi^{+2/3}_2 \end{pmatrix},\ \\
565:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
566:         \Phi_{\tilde{2}} = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\ \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \end{pmatrix},\ 
567:         \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3} = \begin{pmatrix}
568:             \Phi_3^{-1/3} & \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{+2/3} \\
569:             \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{-4/3} & -\Phi_3^{-1/3}
570:         \end{pmatrix}\,. 
571:     \end{aligned}
572: \end{align}

574: 
575: We decompose the scalar LQ Lagrangian as
576: 
577: 
578: \begin{equation}
579:     \mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}} = \mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} +
580:     \mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}  + \mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi} \,,
581: \end{equation}

583: 
584: where $\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$ contains the LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) couplings, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$  the kinetic terms and the couplings to the SM gauge bosons, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}$ the couplings to the SM fermions, $\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) couplings and finally $\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interaction terms. The individual parts of the Lagrangians are discussed in more detail below.

588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}

591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)

614:     \begin{aligned}
615:         \Phi^{-1/3} &\equiv 
616:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
617:                     \begin{pmatrix}

621:                     \end{pmatrix} \,,

623:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

630:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

636:        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}

638:                         \Phi_2^{+5/3}
639:                     \end{pmatrix}\,. 
640:     \end{aligned}
641: \label{eq:ChargeVectors}
642: \end{equation}

644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation} 
651: 
652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}
683: 
684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds
686: 
687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\
692:         \frac{-v A_{1\tilde 2}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^2}{4}\left(\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{(m_{1\tilde{2}}^2 )^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{(m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2)^2}\!\right)&
693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
697:         1& \frac{v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}}{2 m_{2 \tilde{2}}^2} & 0\\
698:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}^{*}}{2 m_{2\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^{2}|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2} & \frac{-vA_{\tilde 23}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\\
699:         0 & \frac{vA_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2} & 1-\frac{v^2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2 }
700:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \,W^{-4/3}\approx\begin{pmatrix}
701:         1 & \frac{v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}\\
702:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}}{\sqrt{2} m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}& 1
703:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
704: W^{+5/3} &= 1 \,,
705:     \end{aligned}
706:     \label{eq:Wmatrices}
707: \end{align}
708: 
709: 
710: where $m^2_{ab} \equiv m_a^2 - m_b^2$ for $a,b \in \left \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$. 
711: 
712: The diagonal mass matrices 
713: 
714: 
715: \begin{equation}
716:  \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^q \equiv W^q \mathbbm{M}^q \left( W^q \right)^\dagger 
717: \end{equation}
718: 
719: 
720: then read~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}
721: 
722: 
723: \begin{equation}
724: \begin{aligned}
725: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-1/3}&\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{1}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{1}\!-\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!\right) , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right),\, \\ 
726:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3}\!-\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\right)\Bigg)\,, \\
727: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+2/3} &\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{2}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{2} , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2 +\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{\tilde{2}}+\!Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\! \right),\, \\ 
728:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3} + Y_{33} \!-\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right)
729: \Bigg)\,, \\
730: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-4/3}&\approx \text{diag}\left(m_{\tilde{1}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{\tilde{1}}, \, m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{3} - Y_{33}\right)\right)\,, \\
731: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+5/3}&=m_{2}^2+\frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_{2}+Y_{22}\right)\,,
732: \end{aligned}
733: \label{eq:LQmassMatrices}
734: \end{equation}
735: 
736: 
737: up to order $v^2$. \\
738: 
739: The interactions of LQs with the Higgs field $h$ are determined by
740: 
741: 
742: \begin{align}
743:     \begin{aligned}
744:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} &\supset \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \Phi^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q}  \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \Phi^q \right)hh \\
745:     & = \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)hh \,, \\
746:     \end{aligned}
747: \end{align}
748: 
749: 
750: with
751: 
752: 
753: \begin{equation*}
754: \begin{aligned}
755:            
756:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-1/3} &= 
757:                 -v
758:                 \begin{pmatrix}
759:                    Y_1  & \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{13}\\ 
760:                    \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}}{\sqrt{2}v}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{A_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v}\\ 
761:                     Y_{13}^{*} & \frac{A^{*}_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{3}
762:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
763:          &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+2/3} &= 
764:                 \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
765:                 -v
766:                 \begin{pmatrix}
767:                    Y_2  & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
768:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & -\frac{A_{23}}{v}\\ 
769:                     0 & -\frac{A^{*}_{23}}{v} & Y_3 + Y_{33}
770:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
771: \end{aligned}
772: \end{equation*}
773: \begin{equation}
774: \begin{aligned}
775:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-4/3} &= 
776:                         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
777:                         -v
778:                         \begin{pmatrix}
779:                           Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
780:                           \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
781:                         \end{pmatrix}\,, 
782:         &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+5/3} &= -v \Big(Y_2 + Y_{22} \Big) \,, \\
783:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-1/3} &= 
784:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
785:                    Y_1  & 0 & Y_{13}\\ 
786:                    0  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
787:                     Y_{13}^{*} & 0 & Y_3
788:                 \end{pmatrix} \,,
789:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+2/3} &=
790:                 -\phantom{v} \begin{pmatrix}
791:                    Y_2 & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
792:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & 0\\ 
793:                     0 & 0 & Y_3 + Y_{33}
794:                 \end{pmatrix} \,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
795:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-4/3} &=
796:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
797:                    Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
798:                   \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
799:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
800:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+5/3} &= -\phantom{v}\Big(Y_2 + Y_{22}\Big)\,, \\
801:     \end{aligned}
802: \end{equation}
803: 
804: 
805: and
806: 
807: 
808: \begin{align}
809: 	\begin{aligned}
810: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,, \\
811: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,.
812: 	\end{aligned}
813: \end{align} \\
814: 
815: 
816: The explicit expressions for these coupling matrices up to $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ are given in Ref.~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}. \\
817: 
818: When listing the Feynman rules for interactions involving LQs of the same charge, we will have to relate the LQ label $a \in \left \{ 1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$ to the position in $\Phi^q$. For this we use the coefficients

820: 
821: \begin{equation}
822:     n_a^q \text{ with } q \in \left \{-\frac{4}{3},-\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \} \text{ and } a \in \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \}.
823:     \label{eq:nqi}
824: \end{equation}

826:

833:      $n_a^q$ & $a = 1$ & $a = \tilde{1}$ & $a = 2$ & $a = \tilde{2}$ & $a = 3$ \\

836:        $q = +\frac{2}{3}$ & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
837:        $q = -\frac{4}{3}$ & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\
838:        $q = +\frac{5}{3}$ & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\

847: \subsection{Kinetic Terms and Interactions with SM Gauge Bosons ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$)}
848: \label{sec:LQkin}
849: The kinetic terms for the LQs as well as their couplings to the SM gauge bosons are presented in this section. The same conventions as for the SM are used. For the three-dimensional adjoint representation of $SU(2)_L$, the $I^{\text{th}}$ generator ($I \in \{1,2,3\}$) has the $3\times3$ matrix form  $(\tilde{\epsilon}_I)_{JK} \equiv i \epsilon_{IJK}$, where $\epsilon_{IJK}$ is the three-dimensional Levi-Civita tensor.  We use the convention $\epsilon_{123} = +1$.

1205: The determination of the Feynman rules to be presented in Chapters \ref{sec:SMInteractions} and \ref{sec:LQInteractions} is carried out using the Mathematica package FeynRules 2.3.36~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}. All model files and the Mathematica notebook needed to display and export the Feynman rules can be found online at GitLab. In the following, the structure of the code files will be discussed. For more information about FeynRules, the interested reader is referred to Ref.~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}.
1206: 
1207: \subsection{GitLab Project}
1208: This GitLab project can be accessed under
1209: 
1210: \begin{center} \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules}{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules}. \end{center}
1211: 
1212: 
1213:  \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules.nb}{SLQrules.nb} contains a Mathematica notebook that is used to determine the Feynman rules and to export them to MadGraph or FeynArts. The FeynRules model files can be found in the folder \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/SLQrules}{SLQrules}. In order to use them, download the entire folder and add it to the FeynRules directory FeynRules/Models on your computer. We also provide prefabricated MOD and UFO model files that can be used in FeynArts \cite{Hahn:2000kx} and MadGraph \cite{Alwall:2014hca}. 
1214: 
1215: 
1216: 
1217: 
1218: 
1219: 
1220: 
1221: 
1222: \subsubsection{Mathematica Notebook}
1223: The notebook \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules.nb}{SLQrules.nb} is used to display and export the Feynman rules. Having loaded the model files, the different parts of the Lagrangian can be accessed via the FeynRules variable names shown in Table~\ref{tab:Lagrangians}.
1224: 
1225: 
1226: \begin{table}[ht!]
1227: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
1228:     \centering
1229:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c c}
1230:          Lagrangian & Variable name\\ \hline
1231:     	$\mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}}$ & LQall \\
1232: 	$\mathcal{L}_{2\Phi}$ & LQ2Phi \\
1233: 	$\mathcal{L}_{kin}$& LQkin \\
1234: 	$\mathcal{L}_{f}$ &LQf \\
1235: 	$\mathcal{L}_{3\Phi}$ &LQ3Phi \\
1236: 	$\mathcal{L}_{4\Phi}$ &LQ4Phi \\
1237:     \end{tabular}\,.
1238:     \caption{Variable names of the Lagrangians defined in Sec.~\ref{sec:LQLagrangian}. }
1239: \label{tab:Lagrangians}
1240: \end{table} \\
1241: 
1242: 
1243: \clearpage
1244: For example, 
1245: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:load]
1246: FeynmanRules[LQall];
1247: \end{lstlisting} 
1248: is used to determine the Feynman rules for the entire Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}}$. The Feynman rules can be exported as UFO files for MadGraph. This is done via the command
1249: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:load]
1250: FeynmanGauge = False;
1251: WriteUFO[LSM + LQall, Output -> "SLQrules-UFO"];
1252: \end{lstlisting} 
1253: The boolean FeynmanGauge on line~1 is used to switch between Feynman and unitary gauge. The files are exported to SLQrules/SLQrules-UFO in your FeynRules directory. We also provide ready-to-use UFO files for $\mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}}$, these can be found under \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/UFO/SLQrules-UFO}{SLQrules/UFO} in the GitLab project. Similarly, the export for FeynArts is carried out using 
1254: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:load]
1255: FeynmanGauge = False;
1256: WriteFeynArtsOutput[LSM + LQall, Output -> "SLQrules-FA"];
1257: \end{lstlisting}
1258: We provide prefabricated FeynArts files under \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/FeynArts/SLQrules-FA}{SLQrules/FeynArts}. Additionally, the export to Sherpa, CalcHep or Whizard is possible. The corresponding commands can be found in \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules.nb}{SLQrules.nb}, but we opt not to include prefabricated files for these applications. The package NLOCT 1.0~\cite{Degrande:2014vpa} even allows for the automatic determination of UV and $R_2$ counterterms, making the export of NLO models possible. We include corresponding commands in \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules.nb}{SLQrules.nb}, but note that these determinations become highly time-consuming for complex models (i.e.~involving LQ mixing). In this work we only consider models at tree-level.
