1293: \subsubsection{Model Files}
1294: \label{sec:modelFiles}
1295: The FeynRules model files are located in the folder \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/SLQrules}{SLQrules}. They are based on existing model files for the SM~\cite{Alloul:2013bka} and the individual scalar LQ representations~\cite{Dorsner:2018ynv}. The scalar LQ fields defined in Ref.~\cite{Dorsner:2018ynv} were merged into the model file \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/SLQrules.fr}{SLQrules/SLQrules.fr} and their interactions with two SM quarks, as well as the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs), LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) and LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interactions were added. The file \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/SLQrules.fr}{SLQrules.fr} consists of three parts: 
1296: 
1297: 
1298: \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
1299: \item the parameter definitions,
1300: \item the definition of the LQ fields and 
1301: \item the LQ Lagrangian. 
1302: \end{enumerate}
1303: 
1304: 
1305: To exemplify (i), a generic parameter definition is shown in Listing \ref{lst:parameter}. The full list of all parameter definitions is given in the \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/README.md}{README.md} file of \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/SLQrules}{SLQrules}.
1306: 
1307: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:parameter,caption=Parameter definition (coupling $Y_{13}$)]
1308: Y13 == {
1309:         ParameterType    -> External,
1310: 	      ComplexParameter -> True,
1311:     	  Indices          -> {},
1312: 	      BlockName        -> Y13,
1313:         TeX              -> Subscript[Y, "13"],
1314:     	  Value            -> 1.0,
1315: 	      InteractionOrder -> {QED, 2},
1316:     	  Description      -> "S3-S1 scalar leptoquark mixing 
1317: 	                           coupling"
1318: },
1319: \end{lstlisting}
1320: \vspace{5px}
1321: 
1322: 
1323: We set the values of all couplings to unity per default. The QED interaction order of $Y_{13}$ is set to 2, since this interaction involves two Higgs fields. An example for (ii), the definition of a LQ field, is given in Listing~\ref{lst:field}. The original fields $\Phi_a$ before the  diagonalization of the mass terms are defined as unphysical fields, whereas the fields $\hat{\Phi}_a$ represent the physical fields in the FeynRules code. In this way, $\Phi_a$ can be used when defining LQ Lagrangians (see below) and the FeynRules code automatically replaces them by the corresponding mass eigenstates $\hat{\Phi}_a$ and the rotation matrices $W^q$

1327: 	\Phi^q_a = W_{n_bn_a}^{q*} \hat{\Phi}_b^{q}

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.

Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. 242: \section{Introduction}
243: \label{sec:introduction}
244: 
245: Leptoquarks (LQs) are hypothetical beyond the Standard Model (BSM) particles that were first proposed in the context of Grand Unified Theories~\cite{Pati:1974yy, Georgi:1974sy, Georgi:1974yf, Fritzsch:1974nn}. What makes them stand out, and defines them, are their direct couplings to leptons and quarks (i.e. they convert a quark into a lepton and vice versa).  LQs were first systematically classified in Ref.~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs}, where ten possible LQ representations under the Standard Model (SM) gauge group were found, of which five are scalar (spin 0) and five are vector (spin 1) particles. While they have received varying degrees of attention since then, LQs have undergone a renaissance in recent years. This can be attributed to the emergence of observed flavor anomalies, i.e. the deviations from the SM predictions measured in several flavour observables. In particular,  $R(D^{(*)})$~\cite{Lees:2012xj,Lees:2013uzd,Aaij:2015yra,Aaij:2017deq,Aaij:2017uff,Abdesselam:2019dgh}, $b \rightarrow s \ell^+ \ell^-$ observables~\cite{CMS:2014xfa,Aaij:2015oid,Abdesselam:2016llu,Aaij:2017vbb,Aaij:2019wad,Aaij:2020nrf,Aaij:2021vac} and the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a_\mu$~\cite{Bennett:2006fi,Abi:2021gix} deviate from their SM predictions by $>3\sigma$~\cite{Amhis:2016xyh,Murgui:2019czp,Shi:2019gxi,Blanke:2019qrx,Kumbhakar:2019avh}, $>5\sigma$~\cite{Capdevila:2017bsm, Altmannshofer:2017yso,Alguero:2019ptt,Alok:2019ufo,Ciuchini:2019usw,Aebischer:2019mlg, Arbey:2019duh,Kumar:2019nfv} and $>4.2\sigma$~\cite{Aoyama:2020ynm}, respectively. Recently, the authors of Ref.~\cite{Bobeth:2021lya} unveiled a further $\approx 4 \sigma$ tension with the SM prediction in the forward-backward asymmetry of $\bar{B} \to D^{*} \ell \nu$. While these hints for new physics are by themselves interesting, it is intriguing to note that they all fall into a common pattern, namely lepton flavour universality violation.

249: Many models that are now being proposed to explain the flavour anomalies jointly contain multiple scalar leptoquark representations~\cite{Crivellin:2019dwb, Saad:2020ihm, Crivellin:2017zlb, Gherardi:2020qhc, Bigaran:2019bqv, Greljo:2021xmg, DaRold:2020bib, Babu:2020hun, Bigaran:2020jil, Gargalionis:2019drk, Saad:2020ucl, Chen:2016dip}. In addition to couplings of LQs to the SM fermions and gauge bosons, also interactions with the particles of the Higgs sector and between the LQs themselves are present in such a setup. In this article, we lay the groundwork for future automated LQ analyses by presenting the complete set of Feynman rules for all five scalar LQs. We include the $\text{LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs)}$, LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) and LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ couplings, as well as all couplings to the SM fermions and gauge bosons. The FeynRules~\cite{Alloul:2013bka} model files as well as the corresponding  MOD and UFO files are publicly available online at \url{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules} and can be used for automatized LQ phenomenology using FeynArts~\cite{Hahn:2000kx} or MadGraph~\cite{Alwall:2014hca}. \\
250: 
251: In Sections~\ref{sec:SMLagrangian} and \ref{sec:LQLagrangian}, we present our conventions by defining the complete Lagrangian for the SM extended with all five scalar LQ representations. Sec.~\ref{sec:methods} gives an overview on the computational tools and in Sec.~\ref{sec:SMInteractions}, the Feynman rules for the SM interactions are listed, while the ones for the scalar LQs are given in Sec.~\ref{sec:LQInteractions}. A detailed description of our treatment of charge-conjugate fermions can be found in~\ref{sec:appendix}.

261: \section{SM Lagrangian}
262: \label{sec:SMLagrangian}
263: The SM fermions and the Higgs field transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as
264: 
265: 
266: \begin{equation}
267: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
268:     \centering
269:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c c}
270:          & $Q^\prime_i$ & $u^\prime_i$ & $d^\prime_i$ & $L^\prime_i$ & $\ell^\prime_i$ & $H$\\ \hline
271:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\
272:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 2 & 1 & 1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\
273:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $\frac{2}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{3}$ & -$\frac{1}{2}$ & -1 & $\frac{1}{2}$
274:     \end{tabular}\,.
275: \end{equation}
276: The prime indicates that these are the weak eigenstates. With this convention, the electric charge $Q$ can be calculated via the Gell-Mann-Nishijima formula
277: \begin{equation}
278: \label{eq:Gell-Mann-Nishijima}
279:     Q = I_3 + Y \,,
280: \end{equation}
281: 
282: 
283: where $Y$ is the $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge and $I_3$ the third component of the weak isospin. The left-handed quarks are components of the $SU(2)_L$-doublet $Q^\prime$ and the right-handed ones correspond to the singlets $u^\prime, d^\prime$
284: 
285: 
286: \begin{equation}
287:     Q^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
288:             u^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
289:             d^\prime_{i, L}
290:         \end{pmatrix}, 
291:     u^\prime_i = \left(u^\prime_{i, R}\right) \text{ and } 
292:     d^\prime_i = \left(d^\prime_{i, R}\right)\,,
293: \end{equation}
294: 
295: 
296: where $i = 1,2,3$ is the flavor index. Analogous conventions hold for the leptons
297: 
298: 
299: \begin{equation}
300:     L^\prime_i = \begin{pmatrix}
301:             \nu^\prime_{i, L}\\ 
302:             \ell^\prime_{i, L}
303:         \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } 
304:     \ell^\prime_i = \left(\ell^\prime_{i, R}\right) \,.
305: \end{equation}
306: 
307: 
308: Note that right-handed neutrinos are not considered in this work. The SM Lagrangian then takes the form
309: 
310: 
311: \begin{align}
312:     \begin{aligned}
313:         \mathcal{L}^{\text{SM}}&= - \frac{1}{4} B^{\mu \nu} B_{\mu\nu} 
314:         - \frac{1}{4} W^{I, \mu \nu} W_{I, \mu\nu}
315:         - \frac{1}{4} G^{\alpha, \mu \nu} G_{\alpha, \mu\nu} \\
316:         &\phantom{12} + i \left(\bar{Q}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} Q_i^\prime\right)   + i \left(\bar{L}_i^{\prime \intercal} \slashed{D} L_i^\prime\right)  + i \bar{u}_i^\prime \slashed{D} u_i^\prime  + i \bar{d}_i^\prime \slashed{D} d_i^\prime + i \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \slashed{D} \ell_i^\prime  \\
317:         &\phantom{12} +\left(\left(D^\mu H\right)^{\dagger} D_\mu H\right) + \mu_H^2 \left(H^\dagger H \right) - \lambda_H \left(H^\dagger H \right)^2 \\
318:         &\phantom{12} - \left(Y^d_{ij} \left(\bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) d^\prime_j 
319:         +Y^\ell_{ij} \left(\bar{L}^{\prime \intercal}_i H\right) \ell_j^\prime  
320:         + Y^u_{ij} \left( \bar{Q}^{\prime \intercal}_i \tilde{H} \right) u_j^\prime + \text{ h.c.}\right) \\
321:         &\phantom{12} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}} \,.
322:         \label{eq:SM_lagrangian}
323:     \end{aligned}
324: \end{align}
325: We use brackets to indicate the $SU(2)_L$ contractions and denote the transpose of a $SU(2)_L$ multiplet $\Phi$ as $\Phi^\intercal$. $B^{\mu\nu}, W^{I, \mu \nu}$ (with $I \in \{1,2,3\}$) and $G^{\alpha, \mu \nu}$ (with $\alpha \in \{1, \dots ,8\}$) are the field strength tensors
326: \begin{equation}
327:     \begin{aligned}
328:     B_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu B_\nu - \partial_\nu B_\mu \,, \\
329:     W^{I}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu W^I_\nu - \partial_\nu W^I_\mu + g f^{IJK} W_\mu^J W_\nu^K \,, \\
330:     G^{\alpha}_{\mu \nu} &= \partial_\mu G^\alpha_\nu - \partial_\nu G^\alpha_\mu + g f^{\alpha \beta \gamma} W_\mu^\beta W_\nu^\gamma \,,
331:     \end{aligned}
332: \end{equation} 
333: 
334: 
335: where $B_\mu, W^I_\mu, G^\alpha_\mu$ are the gauge fields corresponding to $U(1)_{Y}$, $SU(2)_{L}$ and $SU(3)_{c}$, respectively. $f^{IJK}$, $f^{\alpha \beta \gamma}$ denote the structure constants of $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$. $Y^d$, $Y^\ell$, $Y^u$ are the Yukawa couplings and $\tilde{H} \equiv i\sigma_2 H^\dagger$, where $\sigma_2$ is the second Pauli matrix. In our conventions, the Pauli matrices are given by
336: 
337: 
338: \begin{equation}
339: \sigma_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \, \sigma_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} ,\, \sigma_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}\,.
340: \end{equation}
341: 
342: 
343: The covariant derivative is defined as
344: 
345: 
346: \begin{equation}
347: D_\mu \phi = \partial_\mu \phi - ig_1 Y B_\mu \phi - ig_2  \tau_{I} W^{I}_\mu \phi - ig_s T_{\alpha} G^{\alpha}_\mu \phi \,,
348: \end{equation}
349: 
350: 
351: with $I \in \{ 1,2,3 \}$, $\alpha \in \{1, \dots, 8\}$. $\tau_{I} = \frac{\sigma_I}{2}, T_{\alpha} = \frac{\lambda_\alpha}{2}$ refer to the generators of the fundamental $SU(2)_L$, $SU(3)_c$ representations here. The gauge-fixing part $\mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}}$ of the Lagrangian is described in Eq.~(\ref{eq:gaugefixing}). \\
352: 
353: Having acquired a non-zero vacuum expectation value (VEV) $v \approx 246$ GeV after spontaneous symmetry breaking, the Higgs doublet $H$ can be expanded in modes around $v$
354: 
355: 
356: \begin{equation}
357: H = \begin{pmatrix}
358: -i\varphi^+ \\
359: \frac{v + h + i\varphi_Z}{\sqrt{2}}\\
360: \end{pmatrix}\,,
361: \end{equation}
362: 
363: 
364: where $\varphi^+$ and $\varphi_Z$ are the Goldstone bosons and $h$ the physical Higgs field with $m_h \approx $ \SI{125}{\giga \electronvolt}. Expressed in terms of the couplings $\mu_H, \lambda_H$ (see Eq.~(\ref{eq:SM_lagrangian})), the parameters $v, m_h$ read
365: 
366: 
367: \begin{equation}
368:     \begin{aligned}
369:     m_h &= \sqrt{2} \mu_H \,, \\
370:     v &= \dfrac{\mu_H}{\sqrt{\lambda_H}} \,. 
371:     \end{aligned}
372: \end{equation}
373: 
374: 
375: The non-vanishing VEV leads to mixing of the $U(1)_Y$ gauge boson with the neutral component of the $SU(2)_L$ ones
376: 
377: 
378: \begin{align}
379:     \begin{aligned}
380:         \begin{pmatrix}
381:             A_\mu\\ 
382:             Z_\mu
383:         \end{pmatrix} &= 
384:         \begin{pmatrix}
385:             \cos \theta_w & \sin \theta_w \\
386:             -\sin \theta_w & \cos \theta_w
387:         \end{pmatrix}
388:                 \begin{pmatrix}
389:             B_\mu\\ 
390:             W^3_\mu
391:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
392:      \end{aligned}
393:      \label{eq:EWMixing1}
394: \end{align}
395: 
396: 
397: where $\theta_w$ is the Weinberg angle. The remaining two $SU(2)_L$ gauge bosons form electric charge eigenstates
398: 
399: 
400: \begin{align}
401:     \begin{aligned}
402:         W^\pm_\mu &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left( W^1_\mu \mp i W^2_\mu \right) \,. \label{eq:EWMixing2}
403:         \end{aligned}
404: \end{align}
405: 
406: 
407: In the following, $\cos \theta_w, \sin \theta_w$ will be abbreviated as $c_w, s_w$. Instead of using the coupling constants $g_1, g_2$ directly, we will state the Feynman rules using the electric charge $e$. The conversion back to $g_1, g_2$ is easily carried out using 
408: 
409: 
410: \begin{align}
411:     \begin{aligned}
412:         e = c_w   g_1 \,, \\
413:         e = s_w   g_2\,.
414:     \end{aligned}
415: \end{align}
416: 
417: 
418: The masses acquired by the gauge bosons in Eqs.~(\ref{eq:EWMixing1}) and (\ref{eq:EWMixing2}) via spontaneous symmetry breaking are
419: 
420: 
421: \begin{equation}
422:     \begin{aligned}
423:         m_A &= 0 \,, \\
424:         m_W &= \frac{v}{2}\frac{e}{s_w} \,, \\
425:         m_Z &= \frac{v}{2}\frac{e}{s_w c_w} \,,
426:     \end{aligned}
427:     \label{eq:bosonMasses}
428: \end{equation}
429: 
430: 
431: from which it becomes clear that $A_\mu$ corresponds to the photon. As stated above, $Y^d, Y^u, Y^\ell$ denote the Yukawa couplings of the Higgs doublet for the down-type quarks, up-type quarks and leptons, respectively. After spontaneous symmetry breaking, they yield non-diagonal mass terms in the weak basis
432: 
433: 
434: \begin{equation}
435:     \begin{aligned}
436:         m^u_{ij} \bar{u}_i^\prime u_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^u_{ij}\ \bar{u}^\prime_{i} u^\prime_{j}\,, \\
437:         m^d_{ij} \bar{d}_i^\prime d_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^d_{ij}\ \bar{d}^\prime_{i} d^\prime_{j}\,, \\
438:         m^\ell_{ij} \bar{\ell}_i^\prime \ell_j^\prime= \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}}  Y^\ell_{ij}\ \bar{\ell}^\prime_{i} \ell^\prime_{j}\,. 
439:     \end{aligned}
440: \end{equation}
441: 
442: 
443: These can be diagonalized by rotating the fermion fields
444: 
445: 
446: \begin{equation}
447: \begin{aligned}
448: u_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{uL}_{ij} u_{j, L} \,, & u_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{uR}_{ij} u_{j, R}   \,, \\
449: d_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{dL}_{ij} d_{j, L} \,, & d_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{dR}_{ij} d_{j, R}  \,, \\
450: \ell_{i, L}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell L}_{ij} \ell_{j, L}  \,, & \ell_{i, R}^\prime &\equiv U^{\ell R}_{ij} \ell_{j, R}\,,
451: \end{aligned}
452: \label{eq:fermionRotation}
453: \end{equation}
454: 
455: 
456: where $U^{uL}, U^{uR}, U^{dL}, U^{dR}$, $U^{\ell L}, U^{\ell R}$ are unitary matrices, $u^\prime, d^\prime, \ell^\prime$ the weak eigenstates and $u, d, \ell$ the mass eigenstates. The Yukawa couplings in this new basis 
457: \begin{equation}
458:     \begin{aligned}
459:     \hat{Y}^u &\equiv \left(U^{uL}\right)^\dagger Y^u U^{uR} \,, \\
460:     \hat{Y}^d &\equiv \left(U^{dL}\right)^\dagger Y^d U^{dR} \,,\\
461:     \hat{Y}^\ell &\equiv \left(U^{\ell L}\right)^\dagger Y^\ell U^{\ell R} \,,\\
462:     \end{aligned}
463:     \label{eq:YukawaDiagonalization}
464: \end{equation}
465: 
466: 
467: are diagonal and are related to the fermion masses by
468: 
469: 
470: \begin{equation}
471:     \begin{aligned}
472:     \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{Y}^u &= \text{diag}(m_{u_1}, m_{u_2},m_{u_3}) \,, \\
473:     \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{Y}^d &= \text{diag}(m_{d_1}, m_{d_2},m_{d_3}) \,, \\
474:     \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{Y}^\ell &= \text{diag}(m_{\ell_1}, m_{\ell_2},m_{\ell_3}) \,.\\
475:     \end{aligned}
476:     \label{eq:fermionMasses}
477: \end{equation}
478: 
479: 
480: The unitary matrices in Eq.~(\ref{eq:fermionRotation}) can for the most part be absorbed into redefinitions of the fermion fields, the only remaining physical matrix being in the weak charged current for quarks, the CKM matrix $V$
481: 
482: 
483: \begin{equation}
484: \begin{aligned}
485:     \mathcal{L}^{SM} &\supset \frac{e}{\sqrt{2} s_w} W_\mu^+ \bar{u}^\prime_{i,L} \gamma^\mu d^\prime_{i,L} + \text{ h.c.} \\
486:     &= \frac{e}{\sqrt{2} s_w} W_\mu^+ \bar{u}_{k,L} \gamma^\mu \underbrace{\left(U^{uL} \right)_{ki}^\dagger \left(U^{dL}\right)_{il}}_{V_{kl}} d_{l,L} + \text{ h.c.} \,.
487: \end{aligned}
488: \end{equation}
489: 
490: 
491: Without loss of generality, we can therefore assume that the relations between the weak eigenstates $u^\prime, d^\prime, \ell^\prime, \nu^\prime$ and the mass eigenstates $u,d, \ell, \nu$ take the form
492: 
493: 
494: \begin{equation}
495:     \begin{aligned}
496:         u^\prime_{i, L} &= u_{i, L} \,, &u^\prime_{i, R} &= u_{i, R} \,, \\
497:         d^\prime_{i, L} &= V_{ij} d_{j, L} \,, &d^\prime_{i, R} &= d_{i, R} \,, \\
498:         \ell^\prime_{i, L} &= \ell_{i, L} \,, &\ell^\prime_{i, R} &= \ell_{i, R} \,, \\
499:         \nu^\prime_{i, L} &= \nu_{i, L} \,, & &
500:     \end{aligned}
501:     \label{eq:massEigenstates}
502: \end{equation}
503: 
504: 
505: meaning that CKM elements only appear in couplings involving left-handed down-type quarks (corresponding to the up basis). Note that while this choice does not affect the SM Feynman rules, it becomes relevant in LQ interactions with SM fermions. The gauge freedoms of the SM gauge bosons are given in Ref.~\cite{Romao:2012pq} (our conventions correspond to $\eta_Y, \eta_Z, \eta_\theta, \eta_G = 1$ and $\eta, \eta_s, \eta_e, \eta^\prime = -1$). They are fixed using the Fadeev-Popov prescription~\cite{Faddeev:1967fc}. Working in the Feynman gauge, we add the following gauge-fixing terms, after spontaneous symmetry breaking and expressed in terms of the physical fields $A_\mu, Z_\mu, W_\mu^\pm, G_\mu^\alpha$ and their corresponding ghost fields $c_A, c_Z, c_{W^\pm}, c_{G^\alpha}$, to the Lagrangian
506: 
507: 
508: \begin{equation}
509: \begin{aligned}
510:  \mathcal{L}_{\text{gauge-fixing}} &= -\frac{1}{2} \left( \partial^\mu A_\mu \right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}\left(\partial^\mu Z_\mu - m_Z \varphi_Z \right)^2 \\
511:  &\phantom{12} - \left(\partial^\mu W_\mu^- + i m_W \varphi^- \right)\left(\partial^\mu W_\mu^+ - i m_W \varphi^+ \right) \\
512:  &\phantom{12}- \frac{1}{2}\left(\partial^\mu G_\mu^\alpha \right)^2 \\
513: &\phantom{12} +\sum_{B \in \{A,Z,W^\pm \}} \bigg( \bar{c}_{W^+} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{W^+})}{\partial \alpha_B} + \bar{c}_{W^-} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{W^+})}{\partial \alpha_B}  \\
514: &\phantom{12 + \sum_{B \in \{A,Z,W^\pm \}}}+ \bar{c}_Z \frac{\partial(\delta F_Z)}{\partial \alpha_B} + \bar{c}_A \frac{\partial(\delta F_A)}{\partial \alpha_B}\bigg)c_B \\
515: &\phantom{12} + \sum_{\alpha, \beta = 1}^{8} \bar{c}_{G^\alpha} \frac{\partial(\delta F_{G^\alpha})}{\partial \alpha_{G^\beta}} c_{G^\beta}\,.
516:  \end{aligned}
517:  \label{eq:gaugefixing}
518: \end{equation}
519: 
520: 
521: The explicit expressions for $\delta F_{W^+}, \delta F_Z, \delta F_A, \delta F_{G^\alpha}$ are given in Ref.~\cite{Romao:2012pq}.

539: \section{LQ Lagrangian}
540: \label{sec:LQLagrangian}
541: The five possible scalar LQ representations $\Phi_1, \Phi_{\tilde{1}}, \Phi_2, \Phi_{\tilde{2}}, \Phi_3$ transform under the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge group as~\cite{Buchmuller:1986zs} 
542: 
543: 
544: \begin{equation}
545: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
546:     \centering
547:     \begin{tabular}{c | c c c c c}
548:          & $\Phi_1,$ & $\Phi_{\tilde{1}}$ & $\Phi_2$ & $ \Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ & $\Phi_3$\\ \hline
549:     	$SU(3)_c$ & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 3 \\
550:     	$SU(2)_L$ & 1 & 1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\
551:     	$U(1)_Y$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$ & $-\frac{4}{3}$ & $\frac{7}{6}$ & $\frac{1}{6}$ & $-\frac{1}{3}$
552:     \end{tabular}\,.
553: \end{equation}
554: 
555: 
556: Note that we adopt the convention that all scalar LQs transform in the fundamental $SU(3)_c$ representation. Expanding the $SU(2)_L$ multiplets into their components, the following electric charge eigenstates are found
557: 
558: 
559: \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
560: \begin{align}
561:     \begin{aligned}
562:         \Phi_1 = \left( \Phi_1^{-1/3}\right), \ 
563:         \Phi_{\tilde{1}} = \left( \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3}\right), \ 
564:         \Phi_2 = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+5/3}_2 \\ \Phi^{+2/3}_2 \end{pmatrix},\ \\
565:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
566:         \Phi_{\tilde{2}} = \begin{pmatrix} \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\ \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \end{pmatrix},\ 
567:         \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3} = \begin{pmatrix}
568:             \Phi_3^{-1/3} & \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{+2/3} \\
569:             \sqrt{2} \Phi_3^{-4/3} & -\Phi_3^{-1/3}
570:         \end{pmatrix}\,. 
571:     \end{aligned}
572: \end{align}
573: 
574: 
575: We decompose the scalar LQ Lagrangian as
576: 
577: 
578: \begin{equation}
579:     \mathcal{L}^{\text{LQ}} = \mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}} +
580:     \mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}  + \mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi} + \mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi} \,,
581: \end{equation}
582: 
583: 
584: where $\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$ contains the LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) couplings, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$  the kinetic terms and the couplings to the SM gauge bosons, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{f}}$ the couplings to the SM fermions, $\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) couplings and finally $\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$ the LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interaction terms. The individual parts of the Lagrangians are discussed in more detail below. 
585: 
586: 
587: 
588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\
600:         &- iY_{33} \epsilon^{IJK} \left(H^\dagger \sigma^I H \right) \Phi_3^{J\dagger} \Phi_3^K\\
601:          \Big[&- A_{1\tilde{2}}\big( \Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger H \big)\Phi_1 + A_{\tilde{2}3}\big(\Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger \left(\sigma \cdot \Phi_3\right) H \big) + Y_{2\tilde{2}}\big(\Phi_{2}^\dagger H \big)\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\Phi_{\tilde{2}}\big)\\
602:         &+Y_{\tilde{1}3}\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3}\right)^\dagger H\big)\Phi_{\tilde{1}} + Y_{13} \big(H^{\dagger}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3} \right)H \big)\Phi_{1}^{\dagger} + \text{h.c.}\Big] \,.
603:     \end{aligned}
604:     \label{eq:LQ_mixing}
605: \end{equation}
606: 
607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\

644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation} 
651: 
652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}
683: 
684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds
686: 
687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\
692:         \frac{-v A_{1\tilde 2}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^2}{4}\left(\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{(m_{1\tilde{2}}^2 )^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{(m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2)^2}\!\right)&
693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
697:         1& \frac{v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}}{2 m_{2 \tilde{2}}^2} & 0\\
698:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}^{*}}{2 m_{2\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^{2}|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2} & \frac{-vA_{\tilde 23}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\\
699:         0 & \frac{vA_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2} & 1-\frac{v^2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2 }
700:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \,W^{-4/3}\approx\begin{pmatrix}
701:         1 & \frac{v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}\\
702:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}}{\sqrt{2} m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}& 1
703:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
704: W^{+5/3} &= 1 \,,
705:     \end{aligned}
706:     \label{eq:Wmatrices}
707: \end{align}
708: 
709: 
710: where $m^2_{ab} \equiv m_a^2 - m_b^2$ for $a,b \in \left \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$. 
711: 
712: The diagonal mass matrices 
713: 
714: 
715: \begin{equation}
716:  \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^q \equiv W^q \mathbbm{M}^q \left( W^q \right)^\dagger 
717: \end{equation}
718: 
719: 
720: then read~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}
721: 
722: 
723: \begin{equation}
724: \begin{aligned}
725: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-1/3}&\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{1}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{1}\!-\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!\right) , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}1}^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right),\, \\ 
726:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3}\!-\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\right)\Bigg)\,, \\
727: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+2/3} &\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(m_{2}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{2} , \, m_{\tilde{2}}^2 +\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{\tilde{2}}+\!Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}}\!+\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\! \right),\, \\ 
728:  & \phantom{\approx \text{diag}\Bigg(\,} m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(\!Y_{3} + Y_{33} \!-\!\frac{2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\!\right)
729: \Bigg)\,, \\
730: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{-4/3}&\approx \text{diag}\left(m_{\tilde{1}}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}Y_{\tilde{1}}, \, m_{3}^2+\frac{v^{2}}{2}\left(Y_{3} - Y_{33}\right)\right)\,, \\
731: \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^{+5/3}&=m_{2}^2+\frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_{2}+Y_{22}\right)\,,
732: \end{aligned}
733: \label{eq:LQmassMatrices}
734: \end{equation}
735: 
736: 
737: up to order $v^2$. \\
738: 
739: The interactions of LQs with the Higgs field $h$ are determined by
740: 
741: 
742: \begin{align}
743:     \begin{aligned}
744:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} &\supset \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \Phi^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q}  \left( \Phi^{q\dagger} \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \Phi^q \right)hh \\
745:     & = \phantom{+} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)h + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{q \in Q} \left( \hat{\Phi}^{q\dagger} \hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q \hat{\Phi}^q \right)hh \,, \\
746:     \end{aligned}
747: \end{align}
748: 
749: 
750: with
751: 
752: 
753: \begin{equation*}
754: \begin{aligned}
755:            
756:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-1/3} &= 
757:                 -v
758:                 \begin{pmatrix}
759:                    Y_1  & \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{13}\\ 
760:                    \frac{A_{1\tilde{2}}}{\sqrt{2}v}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{A_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v}\\ 
761:                     Y_{13}^{*} & \frac{A^{*}_{\tilde{2}3}}{\sqrt{2}v} & Y_{3}
762:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
763:          &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+2/3} &= 
764:                 \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
765:                 -v
766:                 \begin{pmatrix}
767:                    Y_2  & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
768:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & -\frac{A_{23}}{v}\\ 
769:                     0 & -\frac{A^{*}_{23}}{v} & Y_3 + Y_{33}
770:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
771: \end{aligned}
772: \end{equation*}
773: \begin{equation}
774: \begin{aligned}
775:         \mathbb{\Gamma}^{-4/3} &= 
776:                         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
777:                         -v
778:                         \begin{pmatrix}
779:                           Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
780:                           \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
781:                         \end{pmatrix}\,, 
782:         &\mathbb{\Gamma}^{+5/3} &= -v \Big(Y_2 + Y_{22} \Big) \,, \\
783:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-1/3} &= 
784:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
785:                    Y_1  & 0 & Y_{13}\\ 
786:                    0  & Y_{\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
787:                     Y_{13}^{*} & 0 & Y_3
788:                 \end{pmatrix} \,,
789:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+2/3} &=
790:                 -\phantom{v} \begin{pmatrix}
791:                    Y_2 & Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0\\ 
792:                   Y^{*}_{2\tilde{2}}  & Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde2 \tilde2} & 0\\ 
793:                     0 & 0 & Y_3 + Y_{33}
794:                 \end{pmatrix} \,, \\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
795:         \mathbb{\Lambda}^{-4/3} &=
796:                 -\phantom{v}\begin{pmatrix}
797:                    Y_{\tilde{1}}  & \sqrt{2} Y^{*}_{\tilde{1}3} \\ 
798:                   \sqrt{2} Y_{\tilde{1}3}  & Y_3 - Y_{33} \\
799:                 \end{pmatrix}\,, 
800:         &\mathbb{\Lambda}^{+5/3} &= -\phantom{v}\Big(Y_2 + Y_{22}\Big)\,, \\
801:     \end{aligned}
802: \end{equation}
803: 
804: 
805: and
806: 
807: 
808: \begin{align}
809: 	\begin{aligned}
810: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Gamma}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Gamma}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,, \\
811: 		\hat{\mathbb{\Lambda}}^q &= W^q \mathbb{\Lambda}^q \left(W^{q}\right)^\dagger \text{ for } q \in Q \,.
812: 	\end{aligned}
813: \end{align} \\

816: The explicit expressions for these coupling matrices up to $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ are given in Ref.~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd}. \\

818: When listing the Feynman rules for interactions involving LQs of the same charge, we will have to relate the LQ label $a \in \left \{ 1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$ to the position in $\Phi^q$. For this we use the coefficients

823:     \label{eq:nqi}
824: \end{equation}

847: \subsection{Kinetic Terms and Interactions with SM Gauge Bosons ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{kin}}$)}
848: \label{sec:LQkin}
849: The kinetic terms for the LQs as well as their couplings to the SM gauge bosons are presented in this section. The same conventions as for the SM are used. For the three-dimensional adjoint representation of $SU(2)_L$, the $I^{\text{th}}$ generator ($I \in \{1,2,3\}$) has the $3\times3$ matrix form  $(\tilde{\epsilon}_I)_{JK} \equiv i \epsilon_{IJK}$, where $\epsilon_{IJK}$ is the three-dimensional Levi-Civita tensor.  We use the convention $\epsilon_{123} = +1$.

2662: \subsection{Interactions with SM Fermions}
2663: \label{sec:LQfermions}
2664: The Feynman rules for LQ interactions with the SM fermions are given below. All fields are defined to be incoming. We omit the color indices whenever they just involve trivial contractions. The bar labels an antifermion. Note that while there is an equivalence between a fermion field $f$ and $\bar{f}^c$, stating Feynman rules for $\bar{f}^c$ makes sense in our treatment of charge-conjugate fermions. 6068: \section{Conclusions}
6069: \label{sec:Conclusions}
6070: In this article we provided the complete scalar LQ Lagrangian, including all interactions with SM fermions, gauge bosons and the Higgs. After EW symmetry breaking the mass terms of the Lagrangian are diagonalized, leading to mixing among different LQ representations. We present all Feynman rules, including for the first time the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) and LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interactions. On the computational side, we provided a FeynRules model file containing the complete scalar LQ Lagrangian, as well as a Mathematica notebook to access it. The export to MadGraph and FeynArts is possible and the corresponding files are provided, rendering this a powerful tool for the automatization of studies of scalar LQ phenomenology.
6071: 
6072: 
6073: 
6074: \appendix
6075: 
6076: 
6077: 
6078: 
6079: 
6080: 
6081: \clearpage
6082: \section{Charge-Conjugate SM Fermions}
6083: \label{sec:appendix}
6084: 
6085: \subsection{Treatment of Charge-Conjugate SM Fermions}
6086: Our treatment of interactions involving charge-conjugate SM fermions is based on the method of Ref.~\cite{Denner:1992vza}. It uses the properties of the charge-conjugation matrix $C$ (introduced in Eq.~(\ref{eq:Cmatrix}))~\cite{Denner:1992vza, Nieves:2003in}
6087: 
6088: 
6089: \begin{equation}
6090: \begin{aligned}
6091: 	C^\dagger &= C^{-1} \,, \\
6092: 	C^\intercal &= -C \,, \\
6093: 	C \Gamma_i^\intercal C^{-1} &= \eta_i \Gamma_i \equiv \Gamma_i^\prime \,,
6094: \end{aligned}
6095: \label{eq:Cequations}
6096: \end{equation}
6097: 
6098: 
6099: with $\Gamma_i = 1, i\gamma^5, \gamma^\mu, \gamma^\mu \gamma^5, \sigma^{\mu \nu}$ and 
6100: 
6101: 
6102: \begin{equation}
6103: \eta_i =     \begin{cases}
6104:       +1, & \text{ for } \Gamma_i = 1, i\gamma^5, \gamma^\mu \gamma^5 \\
6105:       -1, & \text{ for } \Gamma_i = \gamma^\mu, \sigma^{\mu\nu}
6106:     \end{cases}
6107: \end{equation}
6108: 
6109: 
6110: to derive two equivalent sets of Feynman rules for internal propagators, external lines and vertices involving (anti-)fermions. The first set corresponds to the expressions 
6111: $\bar{\psi}_1 \Gamma_i \psi_2$ that appear in the Lagrangian, the second set to their charge-conjugate analogues $\bar{\psi}_2^c \Gamma^\prime_i \psi_1^c$. The two are equivalent 
6112: 
6113: 
6114: \begin{equation}
6115: \bar{\psi}_1 \Gamma_i \psi_2 = \bar{\psi}_2^c \Gamma^\prime_i \psi_1^c \,.
6116: \end{equation}
6117: 
6118: 
6119: This double allocation allows for an intuitive treatment of interactions involving charge-conjugate fermion fields. While the underlying principle is the same, our notation differs from Ref.~\cite{Denner:1992vza}. We use two types of arrows on the fermion lines (black and white ones) instead of additional arrows next to them. This avoids potential confusion with momentum arrows as well as having clashing fermion arrows. We proceed by stating the recipe for calculating Feynman amplitudes for processes involving charge-conjugate fermions, which we demonstrate using an example. The Feynman rules for diagrams featuring charge-conjugate SM fermions only are given in \ref{sec:CCFeynman}. 
6120: 
6121: \clearpage
6122: \subsubsection*{Prescription for the Evaluation of Feynman diagrams} 
6123: \label{sec:CCprescription}
6124: The amplitudes for specific processes are determined according to the following prescription:
6125: 
6126: \begin{itemize}
6127: \item Draw all Feynman diagrams for a given process. Two fermion lines with clashing arrows (i.e.~one line ending in a fermion and the other in its charge-conjugate) may be connected by inverting the direction and the colors of the arrows for one of the two lines. It does not matter which of the two lines are inverted. 
6128: 
6129: \item For each internal propagator, external line and vertex write down the appropriate analytic expressions proceeding opposite to the fermion flow. The Feynman rules for normal fermions (black arrows) are given in Sec.~\ref{sec:SMInteractions}, the rules for charge-conjugated fermions (white arrows) in \ref{sec:CCFeynman} and the rules involving both in Sec.~\ref{sec:LQfermions}. 
6130: 
6131: \item Multiply by a factor $(-1)$ for every closed loop.  
6132: 
6133: \item Multiply by the permutation parity of the spinors in the obtained analytical expression with respect to some reference order.
6134: \end{itemize}
6135: 
6136: 
6137: The evaluation of the bosonic parts of a diagram proceed as usual. 
6138: 
6139: \subsubsection*{Example} 
6140: \label{sec:CCexample}
6141: In order to exemplify our Feynman rules, we calculate the Feynman amplitude for the process $e\nu_\mu \to \Phi_1^{-1/3} \Phi_2^{-2/3}$ with an up quark $t$-channel contribution. A similar example is given in Sec.~4 of Ref.~\cite{Denner:1992vza}, which allows for a direct comparison of our notation to theirs. For simplicity, we neglect the mixing among the LQs and take the SM fermions to be massless. \\
6142: 
6143: \begin{figure}[ht!]
6144:      \centering
6145:      \begin{subfigure}[b]{0.3\textwidth}
6146:          \centering
6147:          \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{Example1a.png} \newline
6148:          \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{Example1b.png}
6149:          \caption{}
6150:          \label{fig:Example1a}
6151:      \end{subfigure}
6152:      \hfill
6153:      \begin{subfigure}[b]{0.3\textwidth}
6154:          \centering
6155:          \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{Example2.png}
6156:          \caption{}
6157:          \label{fig:Example1b}
6158:      \end{subfigure}
6159:      \hfill
6160:      \begin{subfigure}[b]{0.3\textwidth}
6161:          \centering
6162:          \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{Example3.png}
6163:          \caption{}
6164:          \label{fig:Example1c}
6165:      \end{subfigure}
6166:         \caption{Feynman diagrams for the process $e\nu_\mu \to \Phi_1^{-1/3} \Phi_2^{-2/3}$ involving a $t$-channel up quark. The up quark fermion lines with clashing arrows shown in the diagram on the left can be combined by inverting the fermion arrows (color and direction) of one of the two subdiagrams. This yields the two equivalent diagrams on the right.  }
6167:         \label{fig:Example1}
6168: \end{figure}
6169: 
6170: The Feynman diagram is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1}. Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1a} shows two parts of the diagram with clashing fermion line arrows for the up quark. In order to combine the two parts, the fermion arrows of one of them have to be inverted. In Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1b}, the arrows of the upper part are inverted, in Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1c} the ones of the lower part. In the following, we will derive the analytic expressions for both of them, showing their equivalence. Choosing the reference order $(1,2)$ for the external states, the Feynman amplitude for the diagram in Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1b} reads
6171: 
6172: 
6173: \begin{equation}
6174: \begin{aligned}
6175: i \mathcal{M} &= \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \left(+i Y_{1, 11}^{LL} \text{P}_\text{L} +i Y_{1, 11}^{RR} \text{P}_\text{R}   \right) \frac{-i\slashed{q}}{q^2 + i\epsilon} \left(-i Y_{2, 12}^{RL} \text{P}_\text{L} \right) u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \\
6176: &= -i \frac{Y_{1, 11}^{RR} Y_{2, 12}^{RL}}{q^2 + i\epsilon} \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \ \slashed{q} \text{P}_\text{L} \  u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2)\,.
6177: \end{aligned}
6178: \end{equation}
6179: 
6180: 
6181: The amplitude for the diagram in Fig.~\ref{fig:Example1c} is
6182: 
6183: 
6184: \begin{equation}
6185: \begin{aligned}
6186: i \mathcal{M}^\prime &= (-1) \bar{v}^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \left(-i Y_{2, 12}^{RL} \text{P}_\text{L} \right) \frac{i\slashed{q}}{q^2 + i\epsilon} \left(+i Y_{1, 11}^{LL} \text{P}_\text{L} +i Y_{1, 11}^{RR} \text{P}_\text{R}   \right) u^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \\
6187: &= -i \frac{Y_{1, 11}^{RR} Y_{2, 12}^{RL} }{q^2 + i\epsilon}  \bar{v}^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \ \slashed{q} \text{P}_\text{R} \  u^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1)\,,
6188: \end{aligned}
6189: \end{equation}
6190: 
6191: 
6192: where the factor $(-1)$ is added since the order of the external states is now reversed. The two amplitudes are equivalent, since 
6193: \begin{equation}
6194: \begin{aligned}
6195: i\mathcal{M} &\propto \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \ \slashed{q} \text{P}_\text{L} \  u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) = q_\mu \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \ \frac{\gamma^\mu - \gamma^\mu \gamma^5}{2} \  u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \\
6196: &= q_\mu  u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2)^\intercal \ \frac{\gamma^{\mu \intercal} - \left(\gamma^{\mu} \gamma^{5} \right)^\intercal }{2} \  \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1)^\intercal \\
6197: &=  q_\mu  u^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2)^\intercal \ C^{-1} \frac{-\gamma^{\mu} -  \gamma^{\mu}\gamma^{5}  }{2}C \  \bar{v}^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1)^\intercal \\
6198: &= q_\mu \bar{v}^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \  \frac{\gamma^{\mu} +  \gamma^{\mu}\gamma^{5}  }{2} \ u^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) =  \bar{v}^{(s_2)}(\vec{p}_2) \ \slashed{q} \text{P}_\text{R} \ u^{(s_1)}(\vec{p}_1) \propto i\mathcal{M}^\prime\,,
6199: \end{aligned}
6200: \end{equation}
6201: 
6202: 
6203: where we have used Eq.~(\ref{eq:Cequations}) and
6204: 
6205: 
6206: \begin{equation}
6207: \begin{aligned}
6208: u^{(s)}(\vec{p}) &= C \bar{v}^{(s)}(\vec{p})^\intercal\,, \\
6209: v^{(s)}(\vec{p}) &= C \bar{u}^{(s)}(\vec{p})^\intercal
6210: \end{aligned}
6211: \end{equation}
6212: 
6213: 
6214: for spinors $u, v$, which can be derived from Eq.~(\ref{eq:Cmatrix}). This equivalence is true for all Feynman diagrams involving charge-conjugate fermions, as argued in Ref.~\cite{Denner:1992vza}. 
6215: 
6216:

35: def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
36:     """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.
37: 
38:     Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
39:     unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
40:     with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
41:     said OK.
42:     """
43:     stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
44:     i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
45:     while i < n:
46:         c = text[i]
47:         if depth:                                  # inside a comment
48:             if text.startswith("(*", i):
49:                 depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
50:             elif text.startswith("*)", i):
51:                 depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
52:             else:
53:                 i += 1
54:             continue
55:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
56:             depth, i = 1, i + 2
57:             continue
58:         if c == '"':                               # string literal
59:             i += 1
60:             while i < n and text[i] != '"':
61:                 i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
62:             if i >= n:
63:                 return "unterminated string literal"
64:             i += 1
65:             continue
66:         if c in _OPEN:
67:             stack.append((c, i))
68:         elif c in _CLOSE:
69:             if not stack or stack[-1][0] != _CLOSE[c]:
70:                 ctx = text[max(0, i - 30):i + 1]
71:                 return f"unexpected '{c}' at character {i} (...{ctx})"
72:             stack.pop()
73:         i += 1
74:     if depth:
75:         return "unterminated comment"
76:     if stack:
77:         c, j = stack[-1]
78:         ctx = text[j:j + 30]
79:         return f"'{c}' at character {j} is never closed ({ctx}...)"
80:     return None

391: def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
392:     """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
393:     texts: List[str] = []
394:     if p.value:
395:         texts.append(p.value)
396:     for r in p.value_rules:
397:         texts.append(r.rhs)
398:     for r in p.definitions:
399:         texts.append(r.rhs)

404: def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
405:     """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
406: 
407:     Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
408:     dependency cycle.
409:     """
410:     names = {p.name for p in params}
411:     deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
412:     by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
413: 
414:     ordered: List[Parameter] = []
415:     emitted: set = set()
416:     remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
417: 
418:     while remaining:
419:         progressed = False
420:         still: List[str] = []
421:         for n in remaining:
422:             if deps[n] <= emitted:
423:                 ordered.append(by_name[n])
424:                 emitted.add(n)
425:                 progressed = True
426:             else:
427:                 still.append(n)
428:         remaining = still
429:         if not progressed:
430:             raise ValueError(
431:                 f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
432:             )
433:     return ordered

439: def _block_entries(p: Parameter, sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> set:
440:     """The LHA entries (index tuples) an External parameter occupies in its block."""
441:     if not p.is_tensor:
442:         return {(p.order_block,)} if p.order_block is not None else set()

444:     for r in p.value_rules:
445:         m = re.fullmatch(rf"\s*{re.escape(p.name)}\s*\[([0-9,\s]+)\]\s*", r.lhs)
446:         if m:
447:             entries.add(tuple(int(x) for x in m.group(1).split(",")))
448:     if entries:
449:         return entries
450:     ranges = [range(1, sizes.get(i, 3) + 1) for i in p.indices]
451:     out = {()}
452:     for rg in ranges:
453:         out = {e + (k,) for e in out for k in rg}
454:     return out

457: def _check_block_collisions(params: List[Parameter], sizes: Dict[str, int]) -> None:

459: 
460:     FeynRules files an External tensor's entries under (block, i, j) and a
461:     scalar under (block, OrderBlock). Two parameters on one entry leave the UFO

463:     define multiple time"). Tensors of different rank in one block do not
464:     collide: GeneralU1's yN[i] and ynu[i,j] share a block and import cleanly.
465:     """
466:     by_block: Dict[str, List[Parameter]] = {}
467:     for p in params:
468:         if p.parameter_type == ParamType.External and p.block_name:
469:             by_block.setdefault(p.block_name, []).append(p)
470:     for block, ps in by_block.items():

476:                         f"External parameters {owner[e]} and {p.name} both occupy "
477:                         f"block {block!r} entry {list(e)}: the UFO would define one "
478:                         "name twice. Give one of them its own block_name (or, for "
479:                         "scalars, its own order_block)"
480:                     )
481:                 owner[e] = p.name

8: 
9: The fiddly Mathematica syntax (association comma placement, ``->`` vs ``:>``,
10: mass tuples, ``Index[...]`` wrapping, rationals) is built here in tested Python;
11: a thin Jinja2 template (templates/model.fr.j2) supplies the file skeleton.
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import os
17: from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
18: 
19: from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape
20: 
21: from .frmodel import (
22:     FeynRulesModel,
23:     GaugeGroup,
24:     IndexDecl,
25:     MassSpec,
26:     Parameter,
27:     ParticleClass,
28: )
29: 
30: _TEMPLATE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "templates")
31: 
32: 
33: # --------------------------- scalar helpers --------------------------- #
34: 
35: 
36: def _bool(b: bool) -> str:
37:     return "True" if b else "False"
38: 
39: 
40: def _quote(s: str) -> str:
41:     return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
42: 
43: 
44: def _strlist(items: Sequence[str]) -> str:
45:     """M$Information-style: single -> "x"; many -> {"x", "y"}."""
46:     if len(items) == 1:
47:         return _quote(items[0])
48:     return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in items) + "}"
49: 
50: 
51: def _name_field(v) -> str:
52:     """ParticleName/FullName/PropagatorLabel: str -> quoted; list -> {...}."""
53:     if isinstance(v, list):
54:         return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in v) + "}"
55:     return _quote(v)
56: 
57: 
58: def _pdg(v) -> str:
59:     if isinstance(v, list):
60:         return "{" + ", ".join(str(x) for x in v) + "}"
61:     return str(v)
62: 
63: 
64: def _indices(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
65:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"Index[{n}]" for n in names) + "}"
66: 
67: 
68: # FeynRules QuantumNumbers holds only additive (U(1)-type) charges. Colour/SU2/
69: # etc. are REPRESENTATION labels fixed by a field's Indices, not quantum numbers;
70: # if left in QuantumNumbers, FeynRules emits an unevaluated `Colour[field]` into
71: # the UFO's particles.py, which MadGraph rejects with "name 'Colour' is not
72: # defined". Drop these reserved index/representation names.
73: _REP_LABELS = {
74:     "Colour", "Color", "Sextet", "Gluon", "Generation", "Spin", "Lorentz",
75:     "SU2", "SU2W", "SU2L", "SU2D", "SU2R",
76: }
77: 
78: 
79: def _additive_qns(d: dict) -> dict:
80:     return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in _REP_LABELS}
81: 
82: 
83: def _reserved_mass_width_names(particles) -> set:
84:     """Mass/width parameter names FeynRules auto-declares from particle Mass/Width
85:     specs. Declaring them again in M$Parameters double-defines the name in the UFO
86:     (MadGraph InvalidModel), so the renderer drops those duplicates."""
87:     names: set = set()
88:     for p in particles or []:
89:         for spec in (getattr(p, "mass", None), getattr(p, "width", None)):
90:             if spec is None:
91:                 continue
92:             if getattr(spec, "sym", None):
93:                 names.add(spec.sym)
94:             for sub, _val in (getattr(spec, "members", None) or []):
95:                 names.add(sub)
96:     return names
97: 
98: 
99: def _is_internal_param(p) -> bool:
100:     """Internal/derived parameters carry a formula (Definitions) that FeynRules
101:     cannot auto-create from a particle Mass/Width spec, so they must stay in
102:     M$Parameters even when named like a mass/width (e.g. a computed decay width
103:     Width -> {WV1, Internal}). Only plain External duplicates are dropped."""
104:     if getattr(p, "definitions", None):
105:         return True
106:     return "internal" in str(getattr(p, "parameter_type", "")).lower()
107: 
108: 
109: def _qn(d: dict) -> str:
110:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{k} -> {v}" for k, v in _additive_qns(d).items()) + "}"
111: 
112: 
113: def _interaction_order(t: Tuple[str, int]) -> str:
114:     return f"{{{t[0]}, {t[1]}}}"
115: 
116: 
117: def _mw_value(v):
118:     """Normalize a mass/width value. FeynRules' ``Automatic`` width is computed
119:     only when AddDecays is on — which is off for us (broken on Wolfram >=15), so
120:     it leaks the literal ``Automatic`` into the UFO and MadGraph fails with
121:     ``name 'Automatic' is not defined``. Emit a numeric placeholder instead;
122:     MadGraph's compute_widths recovers the real width from the model."""
123:     return "1." if str(v).strip().lower() == "automatic" else v
124: 
125: 
126: def _mass(m: MassSpec) -> str:
127:     if m.massless:
128:         return "0"
129:     if m.members:
130:         parts = [m.sym]
131:         for sub, val in m.members:
132:             val = _mw_value(val)
133:             parts.append(f"{{{sub}, {val}}}" if val is not None else f"{{{sub}}}")
134:         return "{" + ", ".join(parts) + "}"
135:     if m.value is not None:
136:         return f"{{{m.sym}, {_mw_value(m.value)}}}"
137:     return f"{{{m.sym}}}"
138: 
139: 
140: def _reps(reps: Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
141:     if len(reps) == 1:
142:         r, s = reps[0]
143:         return f"{{{r}, {s}}}"
144:     return "{" + ", ".join(f"{{{r}, {s}}}" for r, s in reps) + "}"
145: 
146: 
147: def _assoc(pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]], indent: str = "    ") -> str:
148:     """Render ``{ Key -> val, ... }``, dropping entries whose value is None."""
149:     kept = [(k, v) for k, v in pairs if v is not None]
150:     if not kept:
151:         return "{}"
152:     inner = ",\n".join(f"{indent}{k} -> {v}" for k, v in kept)
153:     close_indent = indent[:-2] if len(indent) >= 2 else ""
154:     return "{\n" + inner + "\n" + close_indent + "}"
155: 
156: 
157: # ------------------------------ blocks ------------------------------- #
158: 
159: 
160: def render_information(info) -> str:
161:     pairs = [
162:         ("Authors", _strlist(info.authors)),
163:         ("Version", _quote(info.version)),
164:         ("Date", _quote(info.date)),
165:         ("Institutions", _strlist(info.institutions) if info.institutions else None),
166:         ("Emails", _strlist(info.emails) if info.emails else None),
167:     ]
168:     return "M$Information = " + _assoc(pairs, indent="  ") + ";"
169: 
170: 
171: def _render_gauge_group(g: GaugeGroup) -> str:
172:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
173:         ("Abelian", _bool(g.abelian)),
174:         ("CouplingConstant", g.coupling_constant),
175:         ("GaugeBoson", g.gauge_boson),
176:         ("Charge", g.charge),
177:         ("StructureConstant", g.structure_constant),
178:         ("Representations", _reps(g.representations) if g.representations else None),
179:         ("SymmetricTensor", g.symmetric_tensor),
180:         (
181:             "Definitions",
182:             ("{" + ", ".join(g.definitions) + "}") if g.definitions else None,
183:         ),
184:     ]
185:     return f"  {g.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
186: 
187: 
188: def render_gauge_groups(groups: List[GaugeGroup]) -> str:
189:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_gauge_group(g) for g in groups)
190:     return "M$GaugeGroups = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
191: 
192: 
193: def render_index_decls(decls: List[IndexDecl]) -> str:
194:     lines: List[str] = []
195:     for d in decls:
196:         if d.range_kind.value == "Range":
197:             rng = f"Range[{d.size}]"
198:         else:
199:             rng = f"{d.range_kind.value}[Range[{d.size}]]"
200:         lines.append(f"IndexRange[Index[{d.name}]] = {rng};")
201:     for d in decls:
202:         if d.style_symbol:
203:             lines.append(f"IndexStyle[{d.name}, {d.style_symbol}];")
204:     return "\n".join(lines)
205: 
206: 
207: def _render_parameter(p: Parameter) -> str:
208:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
209:         ("ParameterType", p.parameter_type.value if p.parameter_type else None),
210:     ]
211:     if p.is_tensor:
212:         pairs.append(
213:             (
214:                 "Value",
215:                 ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.value_rules) + "}")
216:                 if p.value_rules
217:                 else None,
218:             )
219:         )
220:         pairs.append(("Indices", _indices(p.indices)))
221:     else:
222:         pairs.append(("Value", p.value))
223:     pairs += [
224:         ("ComplexParameter", _bool(p.complex) if p.complex is not None else None),
225:         ("BlockName", p.block_name),
226:         ("OrderBlock", str(p.order_block) if p.order_block is not None else None),
227:         (
228:             "InteractionOrder",
229:             _interaction_order(p.interaction_order) if p.interaction_order else None,
230:         ),
231:         (
232:             "Definitions",
233:             ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.definitions) + "}")
234:             if p.definitions
235:             else None,
236:         ),
237:         ("ParameterName", p.parameter_name),
238:         ("TensorClass", p.tensor_class),
239:         ("Unitary", _bool(p.unitary) if p.unitary is not None else None),
240:         ("Hermitian", _bool(p.hermitian) if p.hermitian is not None else None),
241:         ("Orthogonal", _bool(p.orthogonal) if p.orthogonal is not None else None),
242:         (
243:             "AllowSummation",
244:             _bool(p.allow_summation) if p.allow_summation is not None else None,
245:         ),
246:         # TeX is a LaTeX label; render it as a quoted Mathematica string with
247:         # backslashes escaped ("\\Gamma_U"), else a raw value like \Gamma_U is a
248:         # Mathematica syntax error that aborts the whole M$Parameters block.
249:         ("TeX", _quote(p.tex) if p.tex else None),
250:         ("Description", _quote(p.description) if p.description else None),
251:     ]
252:     return f"  {p.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
253: 
254: 
255: def render_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> str:
256:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_parameter(p) for p in params)
257:     return "M$Parameters = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
258: 
259: 
260: def _render_particle(p: ParticleClass) -> str:
261:     pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
262:         ("ClassName", p.class_name),
263:         ("SelfConjugate", _bool(p.self_conjugate)),
264:         (
265:             "ClassMembers",
266:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.class_members) + "}") if p.class_members else None,
267:         ),
268:         ("Indices", _indices(p.indices) if p.indices else None),
269:         ("FlavorIndex", p.flavor_index),
270:         ("Mass", _mass(p.mass) if p.mass else None),
271:         ("Width", _mass(p.width) if p.width else None),
272:         ("QuantumNumbers",
273:          _qn(p.quantum_numbers) if _additive_qns(p.quantum_numbers or {}) else None),
274:         ("PDG", _pdg(p.pdg) if p.pdg is not None else None),
275:         ("ParticleName", _name_field(p.particle_name) if p.particle_name else None),
276:         (
277:             "AntiParticleName",
278:             _name_field(p.antiparticle_name) if p.antiparticle_name else None,
279:         ),
280:         ("FullName", _name_field(p.full_name) if p.full_name else None),
281:         (
282:             "PropagatorLabel",
283:             _name_field(p.propagator_label) if p.propagator_label else None,
284:         ),
285:         ("PropagatorType", p.propagator_type.value if p.propagator_type else None),
286:         ("PropagatorArrow", p.propagator_arrow.value if p.propagator_arrow else None),
287:         ("Ghost", p.ghost),
288:         ("Goldstone", p.goldstone),
289:         ("Chirality", p.chirality),
290:         ("MajoranaPhase", p.majorana_phase),
291:         (
292:             "WeylComponents",
293:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.weyl_components) + "}") if p.weyl_components else None,
294:         ),
295:         ("Unphysical", _bool(True) if p.unphysical else None),
296:         (
297:             "Definitions",
298:             ("{" + ", ".join(p.definitions) + "}") if p.definitions else None,
299:         ),
300:     ]
301:     return f"  {p.class_label} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
302: 
303: 
304: def render_classes(particles: List[ParticleClass]) -> str:
305:     entries = ",\n".join(_render_particle(p) for p in particles)
306:     return "M$ClassesDescription = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
307: 
308: 
309: def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:
310:     """Render a validated FeynRulesModel to a complete ``.fr`` string."""
311:     sections: List[str] = [render_information(model.info)]
312: 
313:     if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:
314:         ih = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_hierarchy)
315:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {" + ih + "};")
316:     if model.interaction_order_limit:
317:         il = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_limit)
318:         sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
319:     if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
320:         sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
321:     if model.vevs:
322:         vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
323:         sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")
324: 
325:     for raw in model.raw_preamble:
326:         sections.append(raw)
327: 
328:     if model.index_decls:
329:         sections.append(render_index_decls(model.index_decls))
330:     if model.gauge_groups:
331:         sections.append(render_gauge_groups(model.gauge_groups))
332:     if model.parameters:
333:         # FeynRules auto-declares the mass/width parameters named in each
334:         # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
335:         # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
336:         # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
337:         reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338:         params = [p for p in model.parameters
339:                   if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
340:         if params:
341:             sections.append(render_parameters(params))
342:     if model.particles:
343:         sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
344:     for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345:         sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346: 
347:     for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348:         sections.append(raw)
349: 
350:     for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351:         op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352:         # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353:         # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354:         # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355:         rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356:         for lead in (":=", "="):
357:             if rhs.startswith(lead):
358:                 rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359:                 break
360:         sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361: 
362:     env = Environment(
363:         loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364:         autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365:         keep_trailing_newline=True,
366:     )
367:     template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368:     return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))

710:   feynmangaugerules = If[Not[FeynmanGauge], {G0|GP|GPbar ->0}, {}];

712:   yuk = ExpandIndices[
713:    -yd[ff2, ff3] CKM[ff1, ff2] QLbar[sp, ii, ff1, cc].dR [sp, ff3, cc] Phi[ii] - 
714:     yl[ff1, ff3] LLbar[sp, ii, ff1].lR [sp, ff3] Phi[ii] -

717:   yuk+HC[yuk]/.feynmangaugerules
718:  ];

722:   LGh1 = -ghBbar.del[DC[ghB,mu],mu];
723:   LGhw = -ghWibar[ii].del[DC[ghWi[ii],mu],mu];
724:   LGhs = -ghGbar[ii].del[DC[ghG[ii],mu],mu];

726:   (* Scalar pieces: see Peskin pages 739-742 *)
727:   (* phi1 and phi2 are the real degrees of freedom of GP *)
728:   (* Vectorize transforms a doublet in a vector in the phi-basis, i.e. the basis of real degrees of freedom *)
729:   gh    = {ghB, ghWi[1], ghWi[2], ghWi[3]};
730:   ghbar = {ghBbar, ghWibar[1], ghWibar[2], ghWibar[3]};
731:   generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};

733:   doublet0 = {0, vev/Sqrt[2]};
734:   Vectorize[{a_, b_}]:= Simplify[{Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[b]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[b]]}/.{Im[_]->0, Re[num_]->num}];
735:   togoldstones := {phi1 -> (GP + GPbar)/Sqrt[2], phi2 -> (-GP + GPbar)/(I Sqrt[2])};
736:   LGhphi=Plus@@Flatten[Table[-ghbar[[kkk]].gh[[lll]] Vectorize[generators[[kkk]].doublet0].Vectorize[generators[[lll]].(doublet+doublet0)],{kkk,4},{lll,4}]] /.togoldstones;
737: 
738: ExpandIndices[ LGhs + If[FeynmanGauge, LGh1 + LGhw + LGhphi,0], FlavorExpand->SU2W]];
739: 
740: LSM:= LGauge + LFermions + LHiggs + LYukawa + LGhost;

1029: The charge-conjugate of a fermion field $\Psi$ is denoted as $\Psi^c$, where
1030: \begin{equation}
1031: \begin{aligned}
1032: 	\Psi^c &= C \bar{\Psi}^\intercal \,, \\
1033: 	\bar{\Psi}^c &= - \Psi^\intercal C^{-1}\,,
1034: \end{aligned}
1035: \label{eq:Cmatrix}
1036: \end{equation}
1037: 
1038: 
1039: with $C$ the charge conjugation matrix. A detailed description of our treatment of charge-conjugate SM fermions is given in \ref{sec:appendix}.

1043: \subsection{Triple LQ Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{3 \Phi}$)}
1044: Let us now turn to the LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) interactions. In order to get a $SU(3)_c$ singlet, either three LQs or three anti-LQs have to be combined, since 
1045: 
1046: 
1047: \begin{align}
1048:     \begin{aligned}
1049:     3 \otimes 3 \otimes 3 &= 1 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 10 \\
1050:     \overline{3} \otimes \overline{3} \otimes \overline{3} &= 1 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus \overline{10}
1051:     \end{aligned}
1052: \end{align}
1053: 
1054: 
1055: are the only tensor products of three SU(3) (anti-)triplets $3, \overline{3}$ that contain a singlet. Regarding the hypercharge $Y$, one finds the possible combinations listed in Table~\ref{tab:triple}.

1085: However, not all of these combinations can be implemented. Since the Lagrangian is symmetric under the exchange of identical bosons and the color terms are totally anti-symmetric, the $SU(2)_L$ part needs to be anti-symmetric for identical bosons as well. This is not satisfied by $Y_{112}, Y_{11\tilde{2}}, Y_{\tilde{2} \tilde{2} \tilde{2}}, A_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}3}$ in Table~\ref{tab:triple}. 1092:         + A_{\tilde{1}2\tilde{2}} \ \Phi_{\tilde{1}, c_1} \left(\Phi_{2, c_2}^\intercal i\sigma_2 \Phi_{\tilde{2}, c_3}\right) \\

1095:         &\phantom{12}+ Y_{1\tilde{2}3} \ \Phi_{1, c_1} \left(\Phi_{\tilde{2}, c_2}^\intercal i \sigma_2 \left( \sigma \cdot \Phi_{3, c_3} \right) H\right)

1107: \subsection{Quartic LQ Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$)}
1108: To get four-LQ interaction terms in the Lagrangian, one needs to combine two LQs and two anti-LQs, since
1109: 
1110: 
1111: \begin{equation}
1112: 3 \otimes \overline{3} \otimes 3 \otimes \overline{3} = 1 \oplus 1 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 10 \oplus \overline{10} \oplus 27
1113: \label{eq:SU(3)_singlets}
1114: \end{equation}
1115: is the only tensor product of four $SU(3)_{c}$ fundamental representations $\left(3, \overline{3}\right)$ that contains a singlet. Trivial combinations of LQ fields that contribute to the four-LQ Lagrangian are of the type
1116: \begin{equation}
1117: \begin{aligned}
1118: Y^{(1)}_{a} \left(\Phi^\dagger_{a, c_1} \Phi_{a, c_1}\right) \left( \Phi^\dagger_{a, c_2} \Phi_{a, c_2} \right)\,, \\
1119: Y^{(1)}_{ab} \left(\Phi^\dagger_{a, c_1} \Phi_{a, c_1}\right) \left( \Phi^\dagger_{b, c_2} \Phi_{b, c_2} \right)\,,
1120: \end{aligned}
1121: \label{eq:obviouscombination}
1122: \end{equation}
1123: 
1124:

1202: \section{Methods}
1203: \label{sec:methods}
1204: 
1205: The determination of the Feynman rules to be presented in Chapters \ref{sec:SMInteractions} and \ref{sec:LQInteractions} is carried out using the Mathematica package FeynRules 2.3.36~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}. All model files and the Mathematica notebook needed to display and export the Feynman rules can be found online at GitLab. In the following, the structure of the code files will be discussed. For more information about FeynRules, the interested reader is referred to Ref.~\cite{Alloul:2013bka}.

1360:                                          S1m13hat[cc] 
1361:                                        + HC[W13mat[2,1]]

1364:                                          S3m13hat[cc]}

1369: 
1370: Finally, to exemplify the definition of (iii), the Lagrangian for the LQ-LQ-LQ-Higgs interaction
1371: 
1372: 
1373: \begin{equation}
1374: Y_{\tilde{2}33} \ \left(\Phi_{\tilde{2}, c_1}^\intercal i \sigma_2 \sigma^I H\right) \left( \Phi^J_{3, c_2} i\epsilon^{IJK}\Phi^K_{3, c_3} \right) \text{~+ h.c.} \,,
1375: \end{equation}
1376: 
1377: 
1378: is given in Listing \ref{lst:lagrangian}. Single lowercase letters ($a,b,c$) are used to refer to the weak doublet indices, single capital letters ($D,E,F$) to refer to the weak triplet indices and double lowercase letters ($aa,bb,cc$) are color indices. 1383: L2t33NonHC := Module[ {a,b,c,D,E,F,aa,bb,cc},
1384: ExpandIndices[ Y2t33 R2t[a,aa] Eps[a,b] 
1385: 		2*Ta[D,b,c] Phi[c] S3[E,bb] I*Eps[D,E,F] S3[F,cc] 
1386: 		Eps[aa,bb,cc], 
1387: 		FlavorExpand->{SU2D, SU2W}]];
1388: L2t33 := L2t33NonHC + HC[L2t33NonHC];
1389: \end{lstlisting}

1392: The assignment of FlavorExpand on line~5 makes sure that both $\Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ and $\Phi_3$ are expanded into their $SU(2)_L$ components.

4: Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
5: MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
6: repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
7: predicts takes up to 900 s.
8: 
9: Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
10:   compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
11:   checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
12:   mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
13:   harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
14:   warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass
15: 
16: Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
17: """
18:

22: import re

32: # not be named after (rule 10).
33: FR_SYMBOLS = {"HC", "CC", "FS", "DC", "del", "Eps", "Ga", "ProjP", "ProjM", "T",
34:               "Sig", "PauliSigma", "IndexDelta", "ME", "Index", "Indices", "Mass",
35:               "Width", "Value", "Unphysical", "Abelian"}
36: PROTECTED = {"N", "C", "D", "E", "I", "K", "O", "Pi", "Gamma", "Beta", "Zeta",
37:              "Sqrt", "Exp", "Log", "Sin", "Cos", "Tan", "Re", "Im", "Conjugate",
38:              "Sum", "Block", "Module", "Table", "If", "Which"}

41: _SM_TEXT = SM_FR.read_text() if SM_FR.is_file() else ""

67: @dataclass
68: class Finding:
69:     rule: str
70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None

75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1
109: 
110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None

1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer
tools/frgen/render.py, the lints tools/fr_lint.py and the command ./frgen. Nothing else

write tools, and ONE shell command: `./frgen spec.json`. No other shell command, no web,
no FeynRules, no Mathematica and no MadGraph.

TOOLKIT: `./frgen spec.json` (1) validates spec.json against the FeynRulesModel schema and
prints every schema error, (2) renders model.fr with the deterministic renderer, and (3)
lints model.fr with deterministic rules, each tagged with the stage it predicts will fail.
Run it after you write spec.json, fix what it reports, and run it again until the schema
