588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\
600:         &- iY_{33} \epsilon^{IJK} \left(H^\dagger \sigma^I H \right) \Phi_3^{J\dagger} \Phi_3^K\\
601:          \Big[&- A_{1\tilde{2}}\big( \Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger H \big)\Phi_1 + A_{\tilde{2}3}\big(\Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger \left(\sigma \cdot \Phi_3\right) H \big) + Y_{2\tilde{2}}\big(\Phi_{2}^\dagger H \big)\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\Phi_{\tilde{2}}\big)\\
602:         &+Y_{\tilde{1}3}\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3}\right)^\dagger H\big)\Phi_{\tilde{1}} + Y_{13} \big(H^{\dagger}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3} \right)H \big)\Phi_{1}^{\dagger} + \text{h.c.}\Big] \,.
603:     \end{aligned}
604:     \label{eq:LQ_mixing}
605: \end{equation}
606: 
607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\
609: 
610: The terms in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) lead to mixing among the LQ eigenstates of the same electric charge after EW symmetry breaking. It is therefore convenient to collect them in the electric charge eigenstate vectors
611: 
612: 
613: \begin{equation}
614:     \begin{aligned}
615:         \Phi^{-1/3} &\equiv 
616:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
617:                     \begin{pmatrix}
618:                         \Phi_1^{-1/3} \\ 
619:                         \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
620:                         \Phi_3^{-1/3}
621:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, 
622:         &\Phi^{+2/3} &\equiv 
623:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
624:                     \begin{pmatrix}
625:                         \Phi_2^{+2/3} \\ 
626:                         \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
627:                         \Phi_3^{+2/3}
628:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, \\
629:         \Phi^{-4/3} &\equiv 
630:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
631:                     \begin{pmatrix}
632:                         \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3} \\ 
633:                         \Phi^{-4/3}_{3}
634:                     \end{pmatrix} \,,
635:        &\Phi^{+5/3} &\equiv 
636:        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
637:                     \begin{pmatrix}
638:                         \Phi_2^{+5/3}
639:                     \end{pmatrix}\,. 
640:     \end{aligned}
641: \label{eq:ChargeVectors}
642: \end{equation}
643: 
644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation} 
651: 
652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}
683: 
684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds
686: 
687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\
692:         \frac{-v A_{1\tilde 2}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^2}{4}\left(\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{(m_{1\tilde{2}}^2 )^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{(m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2)^2}\!\right)&
693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}

1293: \subsubsection{Model Files}
1294: \label{sec:modelFiles}
1295: The FeynRules model files are located in the folder \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/SLQrules}{SLQrules}. They are based on existing model files for the SM~\cite{Alloul:2013bka} and the individual scalar LQ representations~\cite{Dorsner:2018ynv}. The scalar LQ fields defined in Ref.~\cite{Dorsner:2018ynv} were merged into the model file \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/SLQrules.fr}{SLQrules/SLQrules.fr} and their interactions with two SM quarks, as well as the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs), LQ-LQ-LQ(-Higgs) and LQ-LQ-LQ-LQ interactions were added. The file \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/SLQrules.fr}{SLQrules.fr} consists of three parts: 
1296: 
1297: 
1298: \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
1299: \item the parameter definitions,
1300: \item the definition of the LQ fields and 
1301: \item the LQ Lagrangian. 
1302: \end{enumerate}
1303: 
1304: 
1305: To exemplify (i), a generic parameter definition is shown in Listing \ref{lst:parameter}. The full list of all parameter definitions is given in the \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/blob/master/SLQrules/README.md}{README.md} file of \href{https://gitlab.com/lucschnell/SLQrules/-/tree/master/SLQrules}{SLQrules}.
1306: 
1307: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:parameter,caption=Parameter definition (coupling $Y_{13}$)]
1308: Y13 == {
1309:         ParameterType    -> External,
1310: 	      ComplexParameter -> True,
1311:     	  Indices          -> {},
1312: 	      BlockName        -> Y13,
1313:         TeX              -> Subscript[Y, "13"],
1314:     	  Value            -> 1.0,
1315: 	      InteractionOrder -> {QED, 2},
1316:     	  Description      -> "S3-S1 scalar leptoquark mixing 
1317: 	                           coupling"
1318: },
1319: \end{lstlisting}
1320: \vspace{5px}
1321: 
1322: 
1323: We set the values of all couplings to unity per default. The QED interaction order of $Y_{13}$ is set to 2, since this interaction involves two Higgs fields. An example for (ii), the definition of a LQ field, is given in Listing~\ref{lst:field}. The original fields $\Phi_a$ before the  diagonalization of the mass terms are defined as unphysical fields, whereas the fields $\hat{\Phi}_a$ represent the physical fields in the FeynRules code. In this way, $\Phi_a$ can be used when defining LQ Lagrangians (see below) and the FeynRules code automatically replaces them by the corresponding mass eigenstates $\hat{\Phi}_a$ and the rotation matrices $W^q$
1324: 
1325: 
1326: \begin{equation}
1327: 	\Phi^q_a = W_{n_bn_a}^{q*} \hat{\Phi}_b^{q}
1328: \end{equation}
1329: 
1330: 
1331:  Such a replacement is defined for $\Phi_1$ on the lines~25-30 of Listing~\ref{lst:field}. 
1332: 
1333: 
1334: \vspace{5px}
1335: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:field,caption=Leptoquark field definition (singlet field $\Phi_{1}$)]
1336: (* physical fields *)
1337: S[100] == {
1338:     ClassName        -> S1m13hat,
1339:     Mass             -> {m1m13hat, Internal},
1340:     Width            -> {W1m13hat, Internal},
1341:     SelfConjugate    -> False,
1342:     PropagatorLabel  -> "S1m13hat",
1343:     PropagatorType   -> ScalarDash,
1344:     PropagatorArrow  -> None,
1345:     QuantumNumbers   -> {Q -> -1/3},
1346:     Indices          -> {Index[Colour]},
1347:     ParticleName     -> "S1m13hat",
1348:     AntiParticleName -> "S1m13hat~",
1349:     FullName         -> "S1m13hat"
1350: },
1351: 
1352: (* unphysical fields *)
1353: S[101] == {
1354:     ClassName        -> S1m13,
1355:     Unphysical       -> True,
1356:     SelfConjugate    -> False,
1357:     QuantumNumbers   -> {Y -> -1/3},
1358:     Indices          -> {Index[Colour]},
1359:     Definitions      -> {S1m13[cc_] :>   HC[W13mat[1,1]] 
1360:                                          S1m13hat[cc] 
1361:                                        + HC[W13mat[2,1]] 
1362:                                          R2tm13hat[cc] 
1363:                                        + HC[W13mat[3,1]] 
1364:                                          S3m13hat[cc]}
1365: },
1366: \end{lstlisting}
1367: \vspace{5px}
1368: 
1369: 
1370: Finally, to exemplify the definition of (iii), the Lagrangian for the LQ-LQ-LQ-Higgs interaction
1371: 
1372: 
1373: \begin{equation}
1374: Y_{\tilde{2}33} \ \left(\Phi_{\tilde{2}, c_1}^\intercal i \sigma_2 \sigma^I H\right) \left( \Phi^J_{3, c_2} i\epsilon^{IJK}\Phi^K_{3, c_3} \right) \text{~+ h.c.} \,,
1375: \end{equation}
1376: 
1377: 
1378: is given in Listing \ref{lst:lagrangian}. Single lowercase letters ($a,b,c$) are used to refer to the weak doublet indices, single capital letters ($D,E,F$) to refer to the weak triplet indices and double lowercase letters ($aa,bb,cc$) are color indices. As described above, so-called unphysical fields ($\Phi_{\tilde2}, \Phi_3$) are used in the definition of the Lagrangian, which are later replaced automatically by the physical fields ($\hat{\Phi}_{\tilde{2}}^{+2/3}, \hat{\Phi}_{\tilde{2}}^{-1/3}, \hat{\Phi}_{3}^{-1/3}, \hat{\Phi}_{3}^{+2/3}$ and  $\hat{\Phi}_{3}^{-4/3}$ in this case).
1379: 
1380: 
1381: \vspace{5px}
1382: \begin{lstlisting}[label=lst:lagrangian,caption=Lagrangian definition (LQ interaction corresponding to $Y_{\tilde{2}33}$).]
1383: L2t33NonHC := Module[ {a,b,c,D,E,F,aa,bb,cc},
1384: ExpandIndices[ Y2t33 R2t[a,aa] Eps[a,b] 
1385: 		2*Ta[D,b,c] Phi[c] S3[E,bb] I*Eps[D,E,F] S3[F,cc] 
1386: 		Eps[aa,bb,cc], 
1387: 		FlavorExpand->{SU2D, SU2W}]];
1388: L2t33 := L2t33NonHC + HC[L2t33NonHC];
1389: \end{lstlisting}

1391: 
1392: The assignment of FlavorExpand on line~5 makes sure that both $\Phi_{\tilde{2}}$ and $\Phi_3$ are expanded into their $SU(2)_L$ components.

7: Structured schema for a FeynRules ``.fr`` model file.

9: This is the shared representation produced by Lagrangian extraction and consumed
10: by the ``.fr`` generator (render.py). Design principle: STRUCTURE the regular,
11: error-prone blocks (M$Parameters, M$ClassesDescription, M$GaugeGroups,
12: M$Information, IndexRange) so an LLM never hand-writes their Mathematica syntax,
13: and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO

16: All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
17: rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.

22: import re
23: from enum import Enum
24: from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

28: # A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
29: NumberStr = str
30: 
31: _OPEN = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
32: _CLOSE = {v: k for k, v in _OPEN.items()}
33: 
34: 
35: def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
36:     """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.
37: 
38:     Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
39:     unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
40:     with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
41:     said OK.
42:     """
43:     stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
44:     i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
45:     while i < n:
46:         c = text[i]
47:         if depth:                                  # inside a comment
48:             if text.startswith("(*", i):
49:                 depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
50:             elif text.startswith("*)", i):
51:                 depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
52:             else:
53:                 i += 1
54:             continue
55:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
56:             depth, i = 1, i + 2
57:             continue
58:         if c == '"':                               # string literal
59:             i += 1
60:             while i < n and text[i] != '"':
61:                 i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
62:             if i >= n:
63:                 return "unterminated string literal"
64:             i += 1
65:             continue
66:         if c in _OPEN:
67:             stack.append((c, i))
68:         elif c in _CLOSE:
69:             if not stack or stack[-1][0] != _CLOSE[c]:
70:                 ctx = text[max(0, i - 30):i + 1]
71:                 return f"unexpected '{c}' at character {i} (...{ctx})"
72:             stack.pop()
73:         i += 1
74:     if depth:
75:         return "unterminated comment"
76:     if stack:
77:         c, j = stack[-1]
78:         ctx = text[j:j + 30]
79:         return f"'{c}' at character {j} is never closed ({ctx}...)"
80:     return None

11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. 13. Flavour structure in matrix form. 77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":

93:     return "".join(out)

96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:

112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]

120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out

129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)

147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:

## Objective
- Extract the complete new-physics content of the SLQrules (SimpleExtensions) leptoquark model from arXiv:2105.04844 and encode it as a `FeynRulesModel` JSON at `spec.json` in the current directory, with `model_name` "SLQrules_gen".
- Run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate per TOOLKIT instructions, and end the final message with the mandatory self-audit table plus one line with the last `./frgen` result.

## Important Details
- Working directory: `/private/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/ob-SLQrules-2p903yoe/`; work only inside it.
- Bash DENIED except `./frgen` / `./frgen *`; use read/glob/grep/write tools for everything else (no `wc`/`ls`).
- TASK.md (91 lines) fully read (re-read this session); self-audit format at line 80; OUTPUT: write ONLY the JSON to spec.json, run `./frgen spec.json`, iterate, final message = self-audit table + last frgen result line.
- Schema rules: all numeric physics values STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on ⇒ `gauge_groups: []`; Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need no index_decls; any other index needs `index_decls` (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); unique `class_index`; `self_conjugate=false` complex / true real/Majorana; External+complex=True forbidden by schema validator → declare new couplings External WITHOUT `complex` flag.
- Charge-conjugate rule (TASK rule 3): ψ^c → `CC[ψ]`, $\bar\psi^c$ → `bar[CC[ψ]]`.
- No EFT cutoffs — complete renormalizable Lagrangian; no 1/Λ terms.
- InteractionOrder decision: `{{QCD,1},{QED,2},{NP,1}}` hierarchy for add-on; all new LQ couplings `{NP,1}` (TASK rule 11 overrides paper's `{QED,2}` on Y13).
- Mass parameters `m1, mt1, m2, mt2, m3`: External numeric strings (gauge-basis masses used in L2Φ terms).

"""
# frmodel.py is a part of the HEPTAPOD package.
# Copyright (C) 2025 HEPTAPOD authors (see AUTHORS for details).
# HEPTAPOD is licensed under the GNU GPL v3 or later, see LICENSE for details.
# Please respect the MCnet Guidelines, see GUIDELINES for details.

Structured schema for a FeynRules ``.fr`` model file.

This is the shared representation produced by Lagrangian extraction and consumed
by the ``.fr`` generator (render.py). Design principle: STRUCTURE the regular,
error-prone blocks (M$Parameters, M$ClassesDescription, M$GaugeGroups,
M$Information, IndexRange) so an LLM never hand-writes their Mathematica syntax,
and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO
bookkeeping) as verbatim Mathematica strings.

All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator

# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
NumberStr = str

_OPEN = {"(": ")", "[": "]", "{": "}"}
_CLOSE = {v: k for k, v in _OPEN.items()}


def unbalanced(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Why ``text`` has unbalanced brackets, or None when it is balanced.

    Mathematica strings ("...") and comments ((* ... *), nested) are skipped. An
    unbalanced verbatim string renders into a .fr that FeynRules stops reading
    with "Unexpected end of file" or "Invalid syntax", long after the schema
    said OK.
    """
    stack: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
    i, n, depth = 0, len(text), 0
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if depth:                                  # inside a comment
            if text.startswith("(*", i):
                depth, i = depth + 1, i + 2
            elif text.startswith("*)", i):
                depth, i = depth - 1, i + 2
            else:
                i += 1
            continue
        if text.startswith("(*", i):
            depth, i = 1, i + 2
            continue
        if c == '"':                               # string literal
            i += 1
            while i < n and text[i] != '"':
                i += 2 if text[i] == "\\" else 1
            if i >= n:
                return "unterminated string literal"
            i += 1
            continue
        if c in _OPEN:
            stack.append((c, i))
        elif c in _CLOSE:
            if not stack or stack[-1][0] != _CLOSE[c]:
                ctx = text[max(0, i - 30):i + 1]
                return f"unexpected '{c}' at character {i} (...{ctx})"
            stack.pop()
        i += 1
    if depth:
        return "unterminated comment"
    if stack:
        c, j = stack[-1]
        ctx = text[j:j + 30]
        return f"'{c}' at character {j} is never closed ({ctx}...)"
    return None


def _require_balanced(text: Optional[str], where: str) -> None:
    if text:
        why = unbalanced(text)
        if why:
            raise ValueError(f"{where}: unbalanced brackets: {why}")


# Mass and width values FeynRules reads: a number, or Internal. The renderer
# also maps "Automatic" to a numeric placeholder. Anything else ("Auto",
# "External", a parameter name) aborts LoadModel with "Wrong width assignment"
# or "Wrong mass assignment", or leaks an undefined name into the UFO.
_MW_WORDS = {"Internal", "Automatic"}
_MW_FUNCS = {"Sqrt", "Pi"}


def check_mass_width_value(v: Optional[str], where: str) -> None:
    if v is None:
        return
    s = str(v).strip()
    if s in _MW_WORDS:
        return
    names = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z$][A-Za-z0-9$]*", s)) - _MW_FUNCS
    if re.search(r"[0-9.][eE][+-]?[0-9]", s):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where}: value {s!r} uses e-notation, which Mathematica reads as a "
            "product with a symbol; write it as \"1.*^12\""
        )
    if names or not re.search(r"[0-9]", s) or unbalanced(s):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where}: value {s!r} is not a number, \"Internal\" or \"Automatic\" "
            "(FeynRules rejects anything else, e.g. \"Auto\" or \"External\"); "
            "use a numeric string such as \"1500.\" or \"2.5*^-3\""
        )


class Rule(BaseModel):
    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""

    lhs: str
    rhs: str
    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"

    def render(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _check(self) -> "Rule":
        _require_balanced(self.lhs, f"rule lhs {self.lhs[:40]!r}")
        _require_balanced(self.rhs, f"rule {self.lhs[:40]!r} rhs")
        return self


class ParamType(str, Enum):

68: class Finding:

70:     stage: str  # compile | checks | mg5 | harness | warn
71:     message: str
72:     line: Optional[int] = None

75: # ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing
76: 
77: def strip_comments(text: str) -> str:
78:     out, depth, i = [], 0, 0
79:     while i < len(text):
80:         if text.startswith("(*", i):
81:             depth += 1
82:             i += 2
83:             continue
84:         if text.startswith("*)", i) and depth:
85:             depth -= 1
86:             i += 2
87:             continue
88:         if depth == 0:
89:             out.append(text[i])
90:         elif text[i] == "\n":
91:             out.append("\n")
92:         i += 1
93:     return "".join(out)
94: 
95: 
96: def _matching(text: str, open_idx: int) -> int:
97:     depth = 0
98:     pairs = {"{": "}", "[": "]", "(": ")"}
99:     closes = set(pairs.values())
100:     for j in range(open_idx, len(text)):
101:         ch = text[j]
102:         if ch in pairs:
103:             depth += 1
104:         elif ch in closes:
105:             depth -= 1
106:             if depth == 0:
107:                 return j
108:     return len(text) - 1

110: 
111: def _block(text: str, name: str) -> str:
112:     m = re.search(rf"M\${name}\s*=\s*\{{", text)
113:     if not m:
114:         return ""
115:     end = _matching(text, m.end() - 1)
116:     return text[m.end():end]
117: 
118: 
119: def _entries(block: str) -> List[Dict]:
120:     """Top-level `Head == { ... }` entries of a M$ block."""
121:     out = []
122:     for m in re.finditer(r"(\w+(?:\[\s*\d+\s*\])?)\s*==\s*\{", block):
123:         end = _matching(block, m.end() - 1)
124:         body = block[m.end():end]
125:         out.append({"head": m.group(1), "body": body, "pos": m.start()})
126:     return out
127: 
128: 
129: def _prop(body: str, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
130:     m = re.search(rf"\b{key}\s*->\s*", body)
131:     if not m:
132:         return None
133:     rest = body[m.end():]
134:     if rest.startswith("{"):
135:         return rest[: _matching(rest, 0) + 1]
136:     mm = re.match(r"[^,}\n]+", rest)
137:     return mm.group(0).strip() if mm else None
138: 
139: 
140: def _is_kin_name(name: str) -> bool:
141:     return bool(re.search(r"kin|Kin|KIN|free|Free|Gauge|gauge", name))
142: 
143: 
144: def term_defs(text: str) -> List[Dict]:
145:     starts = [(m.group(1), m.start()) for m in re.finditer(r"^(L\w+)\s*:?=", text, re.M)]
146:     stops = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"^(?:M\$\w+\s*=|L\w+\s*:?=|\w+\s*=\s*\{)", text, re.M)]
147:     out = []
148:     for name, s in starts:
149:         e = min([x for x in stops if x > s] + [len(text)])
150:         out.append({"name": name, "body": text[s:e], "line": text[:s].count("\n") + 1})
151:     return out
152: 
153: 
154: def _line_of(text: str, needle: str) -> Optional[int]:
155:     i = text.find(needle)
156:     return text[:i].count("\n") + 1 if i >= 0 else None
157: 
158: 
159: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- lints
160: 
161: def lint_text(raw: str) -> List[Finding]:
162:     text = strip_comments(raw)
163:     F: List[Finding] = []
164:     classes = _entries(_block(text, "ClassesDescription"))
165:     params = _entries(_block(text, "Parameters"))
166:     terms = term_defs(text)

168:     term_bodies = "\n".join(t["body"] for t in terms)
169: 
170:     class_names, class_idx = {}, {}

175:             mi = re.match(r"(\w+)\[\s*(\d+)\s*\]", c["head"])
176:             if mi:

178:     param_names = {p["head"]: p for p in params}
179:     index_decls = dict(re.findall(r"IndexRange\[\s*Index\[(\w+)\]\s*\]\s*=\s*([^;\n]+)", text))
180: 
181:     # --- rule 10: names -------------------------------------------------

183:         if name in FR_SYMBOLS:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic lints for an agent-written FeynRules add-on (.fr) file.

Every rule encodes one construct that broke a compile, a FeynRules check or a
MadGraph import in the benchmark (prompt_addendum_v3.txt rules 9-15 and the
repair-loop taxonomy). A lint runs in milliseconds on the text; the compile it
predicts takes up to 900 s.

Each finding carries the STAGE it predicts:
  compile  - FeynRules will not load or will not finish the model
  checks   - the model loads but a consistency check fails
  mg5      - the UFO is written but MadGraph rejects it
  harness  - the validation harness cannot pick the total Lagrangian
  warn     - FeynRules warns; the run may still pass

Library: ``lint_text(text) -> list[Finding]``. CLI: ``fr_lint.py file.fr``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

1107: \subsection{Quartic LQ Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{4 \Phi}$)}
1108: To get four-LQ interaction terms in the Lagrangian, one needs to combine two LQs and two anti-LQs, since
1109: 
1110: 
1111: \begin{equation}
1112: 3 \otimes \overline{3} \otimes 3 \otimes \overline{3} = 1 \oplus 1 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 8 \oplus 10 \oplus \overline{10} \oplus 27
1113: \label{eq:SU(3)_singlets}
1114: \end{equation}
1115: is the only tensor product of four $SU(3)_{c}$ fundamental representations $\left(3, \overline{3}\right)$ that contains a singlet. Trivial combinations of LQ fields that contribute to the four-LQ Lagrangian are of the type

1118: Y^{(1)}_{a} \left(\Phi^\dagger_{a, c_1} \Phi_{a, c_1}\right) \left( \Phi^\dagger_{a, c_2} \Phi_{a, c_2} \right)\,, \\

1120: \end{aligned}
1121: \label{eq:obviouscombination}
1122: \end{equation}
1123: 
1124: 
1125: where $a \neq b \in \left\{1,\tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right\}$. All additional combinations that result in a vanishing total weak hypercharge $Y$ are given in Tab.~\ref{tab:quartic}.

588: \subsection{LQ Masses and Higgs Interactions ($\mathcal{L}_{2 \Phi}$)}
589: \label{sec:LQ-Higgs}
590: The LQ masses and the LQ-LQ-Higgs(-Higgs) interactions are implemented by the Lagrangian \cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy}
591: 
592: 
593: \begin{equation}
594:     \begin{aligned}
595:         \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} 
596:         = &- \sum_{a = 1}^3\big(m_{a}^2+Y_{a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right)\big)\big(\Phi_a^{\dagger}\Phi_a\big)
597:         - \sum_{a = 1}^2 \big(m_{\tilde a}^2+Y_{\tilde a} \left(H^{\dagger}H\right) \big)\big(\Phi_{\tilde a}^{\dagger}\Phi_{\tilde a}\big) \\
598: &- Y_{22} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_2\big)
599:         - Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big)^\dagger \big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{\tilde{2}} \big) \\
600:         &- iY_{33} \epsilon^{IJK} \left(H^\dagger \sigma^I H \right) \Phi_3^{J\dagger} \Phi_3^K\\
601:          \Big[&- A_{1\tilde{2}}\big( \Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger H \big)\Phi_1 + A_{\tilde{2}3}\big(\Phi_{\tilde{2}}^\dagger \left(\sigma \cdot \Phi_3\right) H \big) + Y_{2\tilde{2}}\big(\Phi_{2}^\dagger H \big)\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\Phi_{\tilde{2}}\big)\\
602:         &+Y_{\tilde{1}3}\big(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3}\right)^\dagger H\big)\Phi_{\tilde{1}} + Y_{13} \big(H^{\dagger}\left(\sigma\cdot\Phi_{3} \right)H \big)\Phi_{1}^{\dagger} + \text{h.c.}\Big] \,.
603:     \end{aligned}
604:     \label{eq:LQ_mixing}
605: \end{equation}
606: 
607: 
608: The color indices are omitted since they just involve trivial contractions. For example, the term with $Y_{22}$ in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) would be $- Y_{22} \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)^\dagger $ $ \left(H^\intercal i\sigma_{2} \Phi_{2, c_1} \right)$ in full notation. We use the convention that couplings with mass dimension one (zero) are denoted by $A$ ($Y$). \\
609: 
610: The terms in Eq.~(\ref{eq:LQ_mixing}) lead to mixing among the LQ eigenstates of the same electric charge after EW symmetry breaking. It is therefore convenient to collect them in the electric charge eigenstate vectors
611: 
612: 
613: \begin{equation}
614:     \begin{aligned}
615:         \Phi^{-1/3} &\equiv 
616:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
617:                     \begin{pmatrix}
618:                         \Phi_1^{-1/3} \\ 
619:                         \Phi^{-1/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
620:                         \Phi_3^{-1/3}
621:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, 
622:         &\Phi^{+2/3} &\equiv 
623:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
624:                     \begin{pmatrix}
625:                         \Phi_2^{+2/3} \\ 
626:                         \Phi^{+2/3}_{\tilde{2}} \\
627:                         \Phi_3^{+2/3}
628:                     \end{pmatrix} \,, \\
629:         \Phi^{-4/3} &\equiv 
630:         \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
631:                     \begin{pmatrix}
632:                         \Phi_{\tilde{1}}^{-4/3} \\ 
633:                         \Phi^{-4/3}_{3}
634:                     \end{pmatrix} \,,
635:        &\Phi^{+5/3} &\equiv 
636:        \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
637:                     \begin{pmatrix}
638:                         \Phi_2^{+5/3}
639:                     \end{pmatrix}\,. 
640:     \end{aligned}
641: \label{eq:ChargeVectors}
642: \end{equation}
643: 
644: 
645: After spontaneous symmetry breaking, non-diagonal mass matrices $\mathbbm{M}^q$ in
646: 
647: 
648: \begin{equation}
649:     \mathcal{L}_{2\Phi} \supset - \sum_{q \in Q} \Phi^q{}^\dagger \mathbbm{M}^q \Phi^q
650: \end{equation} 
651: 
652: 
653: are generated with $Q = \left \{ -\frac{4}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}, +\frac{2}{3}, +\frac{5}{3} \right \}$ and~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Hirsch:1996qy, AristizabalSierra:2007nf}
654: 
655: 
656: \begin{align}
657:     \begin{aligned}
658:         \mathbbm{M}^{-1/3} &=     \begin{pmatrix}
659:                                     			m_1^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_1 & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}}^*  & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13} \\ 
660:                                     			\frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{1\tilde{2}} & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}Y_{\tilde{2}} & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
661:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{13}^* & \frac{v}{\sqrt{2}} A^*_{\tilde{2}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_3
662:                                 			\end{pmatrix} \,, \\
663:         \mathbbm{M}^{+2/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
664:                                     			m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_2 & \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}} & 0 \\ 
665:                                     			\frac{v^2}{2} Y_{2\tilde{2}}^* & m_{\tilde{2}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left( Y_{\tilde{2}} + Y_{\tilde{2}\tilde{2}} \right) & -v A_{\tilde{2}3} \\ 
666:                                     			0 & - v A_{\tilde{2}3}^* & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_3 + Y_{33} \right)
667:                                 			\end{pmatrix}  \,, \\
668:         \mathbbm{M}^{-4/3} &=    \begin{pmatrix}
669:                                    			m_{\tilde{1}}^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} Y_{\tilde{1}} & \frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}}Y_{\tilde{1}3}^*\\ 
670:                                     			\frac{v^2}{\sqrt{2}} Y_{\tilde{1}3} & m_3^2 + \frac{v^2}{2}\left(Y_3 - Y_{33}\right) \\ 
671:                                 			\end{pmatrix}   \,, \\
672:         \mathbbm{M}^{+5/3} &= m_2^2 + \frac{v^2}{2} \left(Y_2 + Y_{22} \right) \,.
673:     \end{aligned}
674: \end{align}
675: 
676: 
677: They can be diagonalized by rotating the LQs with unitary matrices
678: 
679: 
680: \begin{equation}
681:     W^q \Phi^q \equiv \hat{\Phi}^q \,,
682: \end{equation}
683: 
684: 
685: in order to arrive at the physical basis with digonal mass matrices. $W^q$ can be calculated perturbatively to arbitrary order in $v$~\cite{Crivellin:2020ukd, Rosiek:2015jua}. At $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ one finds
686: 
687: 
688: \begin{align}
689:     \begin{aligned}
690:         W^{-1/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
691:         1\!-\!\frac{v^2|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{4 (m_{1\tilde{2}}^2)^2}& \frac{v A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & \frac{v^2(Y_{13}m_{1 \tilde{2}}^2+A_{1\tilde 2}^{*}A_{\tilde 23})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{1\tilde{2}}^2}\\
692:         \frac{-v A_{1\tilde 2}}{\sqrt{2} m_{1\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^2}{4}\left(\!\frac{|A_{1\tilde 2}|^2}{(m_{1\tilde{2}}^2 )^2}\!+\!\frac{|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{(m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2)^2}\!\right)&
693:         \frac{-v A_{\tilde 23}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}\\
694:         \frac{-v^2(Y_{13}^{*}(m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)+A_{1\tilde 2}A_{\tilde 23}^{*})}{2 m_{13}^2 m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}&\frac{v A_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{\sqrt{2} m_{3\tilde{2}}^2}& 1\!-\!\frac{v^2 |A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{4 (m_{3\tilde{2}}^2)^2}
695:         \end{pmatrix}\,,\\ \rule{0pt}{3em}
696: W^{+2/3}& \approx \begin{pmatrix}
697:         1& \frac{v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}}{2 m_{2 \tilde{2}}^2} & 0\\
698:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{2\tilde 2}^{*}}{2 m_{2\tilde{2}}^2} & 1\!-\!\frac{v^{2}|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2} & \frac{-vA_{\tilde 23}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2}\\
699:         0 & \frac{vA_{\tilde 23}^{*}}{m_{\tilde{2}3}^2} & 1-\frac{v^2|A_{\tilde 23}|^2}{2 (m_{3 \tilde{2}}^2 )^2 }
700:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \,W^{-4/3}\approx\begin{pmatrix}
701:         1 & \frac{v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}^{*}}{\sqrt{2}m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}\\
702:         \frac{-v^2 Y_{\tilde 13}}{\sqrt{2} m_{\tilde{1}3}^2}& 1
703:         \end{pmatrix}\,, \\
704: W^{+5/3} &= 1 \,,
705:     \end{aligned}
706:     \label{eq:Wmatrices}
707: \end{align}
708: 
709: 
710: where $m^2_{ab} \equiv m_a^2 - m_b^2$ for $a,b \in \left \{1, \tilde{1}, 2, \tilde{2}, 3 \right \}$. 
711:

714: 
715: \begin{equation}
716:  \hat{\mathbbm{M}}^q \equiv W^q \mathbbm{M}^q \left( W^q \right)^\dagger 
717: \end{equation}
